Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade has been postponed, disrupting the holiday plans of the more than 3.5 million people who typically attend the annual event.
The parade is now set for 8:30 a.m. on Saturday, according to a statement shared with NBC, which said the rescheduling was due to weather.
At a press conference on Wednesday evening, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, "I know that many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow," in front of a star-shaped Macy's balloon.
"Generation after generation has watched SpongeBob and Spider-Man soar down our streets and has taken in Garfield floating down Sixth Avenue," Mamdani added. "I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first."
Will Coss, vice president and head of Macy's Studios, said at the press conference that the company was "heartbroken" by the postponement, adding that "this parade has been built with love."
Macy's said in a statement last year that the parade, which began in New York City in 1924, would make its 100th march in 2026.
This is the first time the event has been postponed in its history, and the first time the parade will not take place on Thanksgiving since World War II, when it was canceled in 1942, 1943, and 1944, as materials that would've been used were diverted to the war effort.
Macy's did not respond to a request for comment.

Male, Nov 26: The 8th National Security Advisor (NSA)-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC), hosted by the Maldives on November 25, reaffirmed the commitment of member states to strengthening regional peace and security through sustained cooperation.
The meeting was held at Villa Nautica Paradise Island in the Maldives, with high-level delegations led by National Security Adviser of the Maldives Ibrahim Latheef; India's National Security Adviser Ajit Doval; Secretary, Ministry of Defence, Sri Lanka, Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha; and Commandant, National Defence College, Bangladesh, Lieutenant General Md Faizur Rahman.
Australia and Malaysia participated in the meeting as guests. Australia was represented by Sarah Storey, First Assistant Secretary, South and Southeast Asia Group and Head of the Office of Southeast Asia in the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, while Malaysia was represented by Khairul Azhar (Nik) bin Abu Bakar, Director, Maritime Security and Sovereignty Division, National Security Council, Prime Minister's Department.
During the meeting, the first Secretary General of the Colombo Security Conclave, Vice Admiral S N Ghormade (Retd.), presented a comprehensive review of the actions undertaken to implement the decisions of the 7th NSA-level meeting held in New Delhi on November 20, 2025.
Member states, including the Maldives, India, Mauritius (virtually) and Sri Lanka, signed the Agreed Minutes and adopted the Roadmap of Cooperation for 2026–2027, outlining key deliverables and planned activities under the five pillars of cooperation.
These pillars include Maritime Safety and Security; Countering Terrorism and Radicalisation; Combating Trafficking and Transnational Organised Crime; Cyber Security and Protection of Critical Infrastructure and Technology; and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief.
The meeting reaffirmed the collective commitment of member states to promoting regional peace and security through sustained cooperation.
Emphasis was placed on strengthening collaboration across the five pillars, particularly through training, sharing of best practices and capacity-building initiatives, while underscoring the importance of continued collective efforts to advance the objectives of the Colombo Security Conclave.

UK nuclear test veterans win 40-year battle for inquiry into Cold War tests
Britain’s prime minister has authorized an inquiry into the impact of nuclear weapons tests on military veterans after a 40-year campaign by survivors who say they were used as guinea pigs for tests that damaged their health and that of their children
LONDON -- Britain’s prime minister has authorized an inquiry into the impact of nuclear weapons tests on military veterans after a 40-year campaign by survivors who say they were used as guinea pigs for tests that damaged their health and that of their children.
Andy Burnham made the announcement Tuesday night on the BBC’s Newsnight program, saying the panel’s chairman would be “relentless in his pursuit of the facts.” An estimated 22,000 British military personnel witnessed Cold War-era nuclear weapons tests in the Indian and Pacific oceans from 1952 to 1967.
“Nuclear test veterans and their families have waited too long for the truth, and that’s exactly what the independent panel will establish,” Burnham said in a statement.
Veterans claim Britain’s Ministry of Defense intentionally hid data from blood and urine samples that would demonstrate how they were unwittingly used as test subjects to investigate the impact of nuclear explosions on humans.
Former Defense Minister Tobias Ellwood said in September that he had “inadvertently misled” Parliament in 2018 when he told lawmakers the Ministry of Defense had been unable to locate any information about such blood testing. He later learned that blood samples were taken throughout the military, although veterans seeking compensation for serious illnesses related to radiation exposure were unable to access them.
“This is among the greatest scandals in Britain, and it must be addressed,” Ellwood wrote in the Guardian.
Britain has no dedicated compensation program for nuclear veterans, unlike the United States. France, which conducted tests in the South Pacific and in Algeria, has also established a compensation program.
The U.K.’s first atmospheric atomic test took place on Oct. 3, 1952, with the detonation of a plutonium implosion device in the Montebello Islands off Western Australia. The blast made Britain the world’s third nuclear-armed nation, after the United States and the then-Soviet Union.
The U.K. eventually set off dozens of nuclear explosions in Australia and ocean territories in the Pacific, including Kiritimati, formerly known as Christmas Island.
Veterans’ groups say military personnel, many of them conscripts, were exposed to nuclear fallout when they were ordered to fly through mushroom clouds or watch the explosions without protective clothing.
Campaigners are convinced there is a link between the tests and health problems that they, and sometimes their children, suffered later in life.
Burnham said the inquiry would be chaired by Bishop James Jones, who previously led the inquiry into the 1989 Hillsborough disaster, when 97 people were killed in the crush of fans at a match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest.
The panel will release an interim report by next October, the 75th anniversary of the first U.K. nuclear weapons test, Burnham said.
Alan Owen, who co-founded the campaign group LABRATS, described Burnham’s announcement as a “fantastic step forward.’’
Owen, whose father participated in a test on Christmas Island in 1962, said it had taken a lot of work “over many, many years” to reach this point.
“The campaigners have been fighting since 1984,” he said. “We’re just the next lot of campaigners that have come through to get it over the line.”

Group of Senate Democrats push to add freshman to leadership
A group of Senate Democrats elected in 2024 sent a letter to colleagues Tuesday proposing to add an incoming freshman to the leadership ranks.
"The Freshman Representative to Leadership would be elected by members of the incoming freshman class and confirmed by the Conference," the letter said. "We intend to request a vote on this proposal."
The letter, first reported by Politico, is signed by California Sen. Adam Schiff, Maryland Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin, Arizona Sen. Ruben Gallego, Delaware Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, and New Jersey Sen. Andy Kim.
The letter nods to the diverse class of incoming freshmen who helped catapult the party to controlling both chambers of Congress.
"These freshmen have their fingers on the pulse of long-time Democratic voters, those who voted for Democrats for the first time this past Election Day, and everyone in-between," the letter reads. "The deserve a seat at the table."
Senate Democrats have been signaling a desire to uplift new voices in the party.
"On election night, people voted very clearly for a new generation of leadership. That was very, very clear," Slotkin said during remarks at a conference of Democrats after the midterms.
New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker told MS NOW that leadership extends beyond the top post.
"This is a time for new leadership," Booker said, mentioning wanting to see more of incoming Sens. Annie Andrews of South Carolina and James Talarico of Texas. "I want to see them out front, I want to see them taking issues, I want to see them running on the field."
The proposed rule change comes ahead of the leadership election next week. Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for the majority leader.
Senate leadership is comprised not only of the top position of Majority leader but of additional conference officers. Both Van Hollen and Schumer support the idea of adding a position for a freshman to that leadership group.
"Leader Schumer was already planning to do this and is incredibly supportive of the idea," a spokesperson told NPR.
On Tuesday, Van Hollen posted to social media: "There should be a freshman senator on the Senate leadership team. As I've said, we need a new way to organize so we can deliver for the American people."

Over a lakh persons belonging to high-risk occupational groups, including animal handlers and dog catchers of local bodies, in all 38 districts will receive Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) against rabies under the Tamil Nadu State Action Plan for Dog-Mediated Rabies Elimination (SAPRE) - Vision 2030.
The State government has given the administrative sanction for implementation of the initiative at a cost of ₹2.22 crore, which will be met from the National Health Mission, Tamil Nadu, an order issued recently said.
The Directorate of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine noted that certain occupational groups are routinely exposed to dogs and other animals in the course of their duties. Provision of PrEP to such identified high-risk personnel will provide an additional layer of protection and strengthen the State’s rabies elimination strategy.
The programme aims to provide PrEP to identified personnel of occupational groups having sustained risk of exposure to dogs and other potentially rabid animals.
The main categories include sanitation workers, animal handlers and dog catchers of local bodies and eligible personnel of the Animal Husbandry Department involved in animal handling, dog catching, veterinary and para-veterinary activities.
Eligibility criteria
As per the National Guidelines on Rabies Prophylaxis, eligibility will be determined based on occupational exposure risk and the nature of duties performed. Based on the presently available department data, the preliminary beneficiary estimation was 1,29,009 - 1,21,844 local body sanitation workers, 3,324 local body animal handlers/dog catchers and 3,841 personnel attached to the Animal Husbandry department, the directorate said.
The initiative will be implemented through designated government health facilities, including Primary Health Centres (PHC), Urban PHCs, government hospitals, and medical college hospitals. Identification of beneficiaries and mobilisation will be carried out by the respective local bodies and Animal Husbandry Department.

- A claim has circulated that U.S. President Donald Trump spent his first Thanksgiving as president with the disgraced financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein in 2017.
- The claim appeared to originate with a since-deleted X post by the Democratic Party. The post based its assertion on an email exchange that was part of a trove of documents about Epstein that the U.S. House Oversight Committee released on Nov. 12, 2025.
- In the exchange, dated Nov. 21, 2017, Epstein suggested both he and Trump were in Palm Beach over Thanksgiving that year. The email exchange did not directly say the two spent any time together.
- Trump's official calendar for Thanksgiving as published by Roll Call, an insider publication that covers all things Capitol Hill, showed that Trump was in Palm Beach, Florida, at his private member's club and golf resort between Nov. 21 and 26, 2017, but did not show a meeting with Epstein. At the time, Epstein also owned a home in Palm Beach.
- Reports citing White House officials at the time indicated that Trump would celebrate Thanksgiving 2017 at Mar-a-Lago, the private member's club he reportedly kicked Epstein out of 10 years prior. It was unclear who did attend Trump's Thanksgiving celebrations.
- White House spokesperson Abigail Jackson did not reply to a query about whether Trump spent time with Epstein during Thanksgiving 2017, instead writing, "These emails prove literally nothing."
Ahead of Thanksgiving, a claim (archived) circulated online that U.S. President Donald Trump spent his first Thanksgiving as president in 2017 with the disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.
Snopes previously reported on this claim in November 2025, when questions about Trump's whereabouts coincided with the House Oversight Committee's release of a trove of documents relating to Epstein, a sex offender who died in a New York City jail cell in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex-trafficking charges.
Trump and Epstein had a well-documented friendship in the early 2000s. The exact circumstances of how the friendship ended remained unclear. Trump reportedly kicked Epstein out of his Mar-a-Lago club in 2007, 10 years before online claims said the pair spent Thanksgiving together.
One Threads user who spread the claim about Epstein and Trump spending Thanksgiving 2017 together wrote, "The NEW 20,000 Epstein Files released yesterday, SHOW TRUMP HAVING THANKSGIVING DINNER WITH EPSTEIN (WHILE IN THE WHITE HOUSE 2017)"
The claim also circulated on Facebook (archived).
It appeared to originate with a post on the @TheDemocrats X account, the official account of the Democratic Party. According to screenshots of it (archived, archived), that post claimed an email exchange from the House Oversight Committee release showed that Trump spent Thanksgiving with Epstein in 2017. The post did not appear on the @TheDemocrats X account at the time of this writing.
The email exchange the post referred to between Epstein and Faith Kates, reportedly a fashion management executive, did suggest that Epstein and Trump were both in or near Palm Beach, Florida, during Thanksgiving 2017. At the time, Epstein owned a mansion in Palm Beach. According to Roll Call's public schedule for the president, Trump spent five days at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach from Nov. 21 to 26, 2017. Roll Call is an insider publication that covers all things Capitol Hill.
In the released email exchange dated Nov. 23, 2017, Kates asked Epstein "When are you back in NYC?" suggesting that Epstein was not at his Manhattan townhouse. Later in the exchange, Kates asked, "Who else is down there?" to which Epstein replied, "david fizel, hanson. trump." Given that Roll Call's Presidential Calendar and reports at the time said Trump was in Mar-a-Lago, the email exchange suggested "down there" meant Palm Beach.
While both Epstein and Trump were likely in Palm Beach over Thanksgiving 2017 (the holiday fell on Nov. 23 that year), Epstein did not directly say in the email exchange that he had or would spend time with the president while in Florida. We did not find other reputable reports that Epstein and Trump spent time together during Thanksgiving 2017. Due to the possibility of a private meeting between the two, we leave this claim unrated.
White House spokeswoman Abigail Jackson did not reply to an emailed question about whether Trump spent time with Epstein during Thanksgiving 2017. Instead, Jackson said via email when we first investigated this claim in 2025: "These emails prove literally nothing. Democrats and the mainstream media are desperately trying to use this hoax as a distraction to talk about anything other than Democrats getting utterly defeated by President Trump in the [2025 government] shutdown fight."
Snopes reached out to communications staff at the Democratic National Committee, which runs the @TheDemocrats X account, to confirm whether it posted and deleted the X post in question, and why. We also reached out to Kates to confirm her role in the correspondence and whether Epstein told her he spent Thanksgiving with Trump. We reached out again in 2026 and await replies to our queries.
Trump's calendar did not show meeting with Epstein
According to Roll Call and reports at the time, Trump arrived at Palm Beach International Airport the afternoon of Nov. 21, 2017. He had no public events scheduled on Nov. 22, but met with pool reporters in the morning and went to Trump International Golf Club around 9:30 a.m., according to Roll Call. Trump posted (archived) on X on Nov. 22 that he would be "having meetings and working the phones from the Winter White House in Florida (Mar-a-Lago)."
On Thanksgiving, Nov. 23, Roll Call's calendar showed Trump thanked members of the military on a virtual call and visited Coast Guard members at Lake Worth Inlet Station before heading back to Trump International Golf Club around 11 a.m. News reports and official records corroborated the two Nov. 23 engagements in or near Palm Beach.
Trump had no public events scheduled on Nov. 24, 25 or 26, according to Roll Call. He reportedly played golf with professional golfers Tiger Woods and Dustin Johnson on Nov. 24.
Much of the time Trump spent in Palm Beach was unaccounted for in Roll Call's calendar. According to a CNN report at the time that cited White House spokespeople, Trump planned to celebrate the holiday with family at Mar-a-Lago. It was unclear exactly who attended festivities at Mar-a-Lago.
According to a Guardian analysis of the House Oversight Committee's document release, Epstein stayed informed about Trump's travel as it related to his own after the pair fell out. The Guardian reported that Epstein would discuss Trump's travel with employees as both regularly flew in and out of Palm Beach International Airport.
According to the report, Epstein continued to discuss Trump's whereabouts in New York City and Palm Beach and received news articles about Trump more generally from his associates after the two fell out and Trump became president.
Snopes previously reported on the content of the House Oversight Committee's email release, including whether Epstein called Trump "the dog that hasn't barked" or alleged Trump "knew about the girls," referring to victims of Epstein's alleged sex crimes.

The fetishization of mass murderers has been around since long before TikTok.
Bonnie and Clyde were folk heroes. Serial killer Ted Bundy was adored by a legion of female fans. And the mother of Columbine shooter Dylan Klebold reported receiving love letters to her son in the mail written by young girls.
More recently, this phenomenon has manifested in a network known as the True Crime Community, or TCC, a group of mainly young people who lionize mass shooters like Klebold. (This group is distinct from true crime enthusiasts who like to read books or listen to podcasts about unsolved crimes.)
While this community has been around for years, in 2026, it moved en masse to TikTok. There, supercharged by the video-sharing platform's powerful black-box algorithm, the community’s violent, nihilistic worldview expanded its reach dramatically, serving up graphic content to users who had never been exposed before.
Tracking the scale and real-world impact of the network has been difficult, because the coded language, symbols, and memes used within the group are constantly changing to avoid detection by platforms and law enforcement. On TikTok some of the group members most interested in violence began referring to the group as the True Cringe Community. When TikTok blocked that term, they began referring to themselves as the True Larp Community.
But now, for the first time, the National Contagion Research Institute (NCRI), a Princeton, New Jersey–based nonprofit that tracks online extremism, has collated data that shows that attacks and attempted attacks linked to the TCC have exploded by 200 percent over the last two years. The data, shared exclusively with WIRED ahead of publication, shows that the number of annual attacks or attempted attacks have gone from 13 reported in all of 2024 to 30 by mid-October this year.
The footprint of these attacks also expanded globally. Attacks and attempted attacks linked to the TCC were registered in 13 different countries in 2026, with two of every three incidents happening outside the US. And NCRI’s researchers predict that without intervention, the situation is about to get much worse.
“This is heading towards an explosion,” Joel Finkelstein, chief science officer with NCRI, tells WIRED. “That's what the data is suggesting, and the data is unambiguous. It's heading next year to a point where this is going to be happening more than once a week. That's really alarming.”
The TCC is part of a broader online nihilistic violent extremism movement and often overlaps with the extremist crime network known as “The Com,” which incorporates groups like 764 and No Lives Matter,
The TCC’s members, a large proportion of which are teenagers, share content online that references, glorifies, mimics, and simulates school shooters, mass shooters, and serial killers from all over the world. This is done through flattering videos posted on social media, taking pictures replicating the hand signals attackers used during their killing sprees, or wearing the T-shirts worn by mass shooters. The members also use AI to turn videos of mass shootings into cartoons or anime in order to avoid detection by online platforms’ trust and safety teams.
Beyond posting fan fiction about their favorite school shooters, this community also encourages others to carry out their own attacks. If successful, those attackers in turn become part of TCC’s ever-expanding lore and mythology, becoming part of a self-reinforcing cycle.
While writing its report, NCRI researchers documented numerous other attacks linked to the group, including the September 18 shooting at a high school in the Philippines and an October 1 attack at a secondary school in Torreón, Mexico. There was also a shooting on October 12 at a middle school in France and a knife attack on October 13 in South Africa that have also been linked to the TCC community.
While TCC was found on a lot of platforms online, for the first 10 years of its existence, much of its activity was centered on Tumblr. But in January, the site implemented a ban wave that drove much of the community to TikTok, where the platform’s unique algorithm put TCC-related content in front of a much broader audience, according to a report from the Institute of Strategic Dialogue published earlier this month.
“Algorithmically driven engagement has supercharged its spread,” the report’s authors wrote. “Unlike Tumblr, where the fandom is largely isolated, TikTok actively works to expose users to new content through its algorithm, resulting in TCC videos being served to a much larger audience.”
Finkelstein says that while TikTok does remove some of the accounts his team flags to the platform, in general the company is not doing enough to combat the problem.
“[TikTok’s] capacity to manage this is very spotty,” Finkelstein said. “This is an uncontained open wound. Whatever measures they think they're making to manage this are obviously inadequate to deal with the damage that the community is unleashing. If you took TikTok offline for a few weeks, my guess is these attacks would slow down because there's not a permission structure in place that's encouraging vulnerable youth to go out and murder people in order to be famous with their peers because they're so depressed and living in their mom's basement and spending 10 hours a day on social media.”
TikTok, whose US operations are now owned primarily by a group of investors including Oracle, controlled by GOP megadonor and Donald Trump ally Larry Ellison, said it had rules in place to proactively remove TCC-linked content.
“We enforce strict rules against content that promotes violence or glorifies perpetrators of mass violence, and we had already banned a large number of the accounts in this report,” a TikTok spokesperson tells WIRED.
WIRED shared the report with several other researchers who closely track TCC activity online, and all broadly concluded that NCRI’s assessment was accurate. One independent researcher, Ry Terran, pointed out that accurately tracking this movement is difficult given the dense nature of the language they use around attacks.
“When examining perpetrators' social media, I see that they frequently frame threats as a joke, a LARP, or AI-generated,” Terran tells WIRED. “Social media companies should not take these claims at face value, but rather report any credible threats. Without appropriate interventions, TCC-inspired attacks will likely continue to increase.”
Another European-based researcher, who requested anonymity due to fears of retaliation, tells WIRED, “We're panicking here in Europe.” The researcher collaborates with European law enforcement agencies and says they are concerned about the increasing number of attacks taking place globally.
Finkelstein says that US lawmakers and law enforcement need to do more in order to combat this problem. “The FBI seems to want to deal with it by arresting kids. None of this makes any sense,” he says. “We've got to step back and see the scale of this. We should be turning to our law enforcement agencies and our national security apparatus that has the ear of the president and say something's got to be done about this.”
The FBI declined to comment, and the White House did not respond to a request for comment. The Department of Homeland Security referred WIRED to the FBI.
“The Justice Department remains vigilant against the threat of such violent extremist networks that operate within the United States and around the globe,” Wyn Hornbuckle, a spokesman for the Department of Justice, tells WIRED.

Why the Army detonated toxic explosives in Iowa
It was probably the least bad option.
On Wednesday, the Pentagon blew up about five tons of lead azide, an unstable explosive stored at an ammunition plant in Iowa, in order to dispose of it, sending a toxic plume of lead dust into the sky the day before Thanksgiving.
The detonation was briefly halted by a lower court before a federal circuit court cleared the way on Monday, and went forward despite serious public health concerns.
There was a real need for haste, according to the Army: The lead azide was sufficiently unstable that it was at risk of detonating on its own in an uncontrolled explosion, and falling temperatures in Iowa reportedly made such an explosion more likely. An uncontrolled explosion would have be more dangerous and unpredictable, and could have caused worse lead pollution.
At the same time, though, Iowa residents are angry and alarmed by a lack of clear information, poor communication by the Army, and the potential health hazards.
The potential for things to go sideways had President Donald Trump nervous enough that he tried to pass the decision to Rob Sand — not the current Iowa governor, but the incoming Democratic governor-elect — and let any consequences fall on his head.
The lead plume produced by the blast — which will take place inside reinforced concrete bunkers, along with other steps to mitigate the risk — could still spread as far as 100 miles from the site, according to the Washington Post.
The American Lung Association has urged anyone near the blast to remain inside for one to two days afterward, among other guidance, and on Tuesday, the Health and Human Services Department recommended that children and pregnant women evacuate from the path of the plume, which could stretch into neighboring Missouri.
The lead risk all around us
Emergency munitions detonations in the US are pretty rare — there are, thankfully, better ways to dispose of toxic materials these days (and questions about why the Army didn’t pursue them in this case).
But despite a great deal of progress in the US — including banning things like new lead paint and pipes and leaded gasoline in the 20th century — lead remains a serious public health threat.
Part of that is because of how dangerous it really is: Lead is not just a neurotoxin, but one with no safe levels of human exposure; even a little bit can be harmful, especially to children.
But as my colleague Dylan Scott reported in 2024, it also keeps popping up nearly everywhere we look, including in our food supply.
According to Dylan’s reporting, there are three big reasons for lead’s seeming inescapability: Active disregard, negligence, and the fact that it’s just really hard to get rid of. Lead was widely used in the US decades ago, before those bans on lead paint and leaded gasoline, and some of that lead is still around, in the soil, in old houses, and in other materials dating back to that time.
It’s also not a problem that the US can easily address alone, since lots of lead exposure is the result of goods being imported into the US.
“If we really want to solve this,” Drew McCartor, the director of a global public health nonprofit, told Dylan at the time, “it requires a whole-of-government commitment to work outside of our borders.”
One link for later
➨ Follow “Maslow’s hierarchy of hosting.” Thanksgiving is almost upon us, and if you’re feeling a little angsty about your holiday obligations, consider this guidance from the event planner Megan Fitzgerald: Your hosting needs, at a minimum, start with a clean space, a bathroom stocked with adequate toilet paper, and enough cups and water to go around. (Plus, of course, the food.) Basically, everything else is extra.
Before you go…
- Did you know…that, with very few exceptions, US grocery stores sell only one breed of turkey? It’s called the Broad Breasted White turkey, and it’s been bred to grow twice as fast (and become nearly twice as big) as its forebears did in the 1960s.

The Delhi High Court, on Thursday, ordered that the results of the All India Tennis Association (AITA) elections scheduled to be held on November 27 in Ahmedabad be kept in a sealed cover until the next date of hearing (December 14).
The bench headed by acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre also made it clear that no policy rulings or major financial decisions can be taken by the AITA until the case is heard again.
The order was passed after a plea to stay the elections was filed earlier this week by former players Somdev Devvarman and Purav Raja, the original petitioners in the long-running saga.
Clubbed with the stay request was the application filed on November 17 by Justice (retd.) Gita Mittal, the administrator appointed by the High Court in April 2026 to oversee the affairs of the AITA until a new body took over.
Justice Mittal had alleged “violation of judicial mandate and unilateral usurpation of authority and power by the interim Executive Committee of the appellant (AITA)”.
Justice Sambre stated that even as interim EC claimed to have appointed the Electoral Officer in accordance to the amended AITA Constitution, the Court was of the view that it had to be done under the aegis of Justice Mittal.
“We see no prima facie reason to permit the appellant (AITA) to appoint the election officer,” Justice Sambre declared in open court, citing the judgment from April 2026 which had clearly laid out the administrator’s responsibilities.

Mushroom supplements promise health benefits. What does the science say?
Growing up in the French Alps, Julie Daoust fell for mushrooms early in life.
"So as a kid, we'd go out and forage," she recalls. "We'd come across species like lion's mane or reishi. And I became more and more interested in those species."
Daoust went on to get a Ph.D. in chemistry, searching nature for novel pharmaceuticals. Her work ultimately led her back to mushrooms, a group of organisms to which humans are more closely related than plants. And yet, many of our modern medicines and therapeutics come from plants.
"Mushrooms share a lot more in terms of their biochemistry with us than plants do," says Daoust, which means "you have more chances of finding something that's going to have bioactivity in a human than you would with other source organisms."
Daoust is now vice president of science and innovation at Monterey Nutra, a company that specializes in the genetics and cultivation of mushrooms and sells fungal extracts and powders. Her team focuses not on the poisonous varieties, nor the psychedelic ones that contain psilocybin. Rather, they are interested in the functional or medicinal mushrooms that Daoust likens to tiny cauldrons of potentially useful molecules.
"We love to look for soft things that can't run away very fast," says Daoust, "because they typically produce really interesting chemistry to defend themselves or to communicate with others in their environment to survive."
The claim
Daoust says that certain types of fungi may have specific uses.
For instance, lion's mane — a soft chandelier of a fungus — may aid cognition. Reishi and turkey tail, which are mushrooms that grow as hard brown scales on decomposing trees, could bolster immune health.
And on social media, influencers and advertisers promise that medicinal mushrooms, taken as supplements, can slow aging and improve energy levels, focus and immune health.
The evidence
Robust clinical trials proving such connections — and their safety — are largely lacking, according to Abby Langer, a registered dietitian based in Toronto. "In my opinion, I don't think that there's much evidence for functional mushrooms as of now," she says.
Langer says mushrooms accumulate and concentrate the materials in the ground they're grown in, both good and bad — so one has to be cautious.
Want the latest stories on the science of healthy living? Subscribe to NPR's Health newsletter.
She grants that in certain communities (in parts of Asia, for instance), mushrooms have been incorporated into their healing practices for generations. However, "just because something has been used for a long time doesn't mean that it's safe, that it's effective, that the dosing has been established," Langer says. "There are a lot of unknowns."
Still, she acknowledges that empirical support for the potential positive impacts of mushrooms is growing. "The clinical research on specific functional mushroom products is young," she says, "but it's accumulating fast and already includes some impressive results."
Mushrooms are a good source of vitamin D2 and antioxidants. Their cell walls contain beta-glucan, which has been linked to gut health, including a lower risk of Crohn's Disease, and immune response. Research into the effects of mushrooms on cognition have been mixed.
In addition, there's work out of Japan looking at how PSK, a purified extract from turkey tail, improved immune response in cancer patients. A meta-analysis considered 8,009 patients in eight randomized controlled trials who had undergone surgical removal of a gastric tumor and in almost all cases chemotherapy. Those who were also given PSK showed a 12% reduction in risk of death.
"This is not something that we brush off," says Santhosshi Narayanan, an integrative oncologist based at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center who recognizes the potential of PSK.
Even so, she admits that this "does not mean that PSK or any mushrooms alone cures cancer. It just shows to us that we need to pay attention to these natural products." Narayanan says there's still a lot to figure out with this particular extract, especially for populations outside Japan with different genetics or treatment regimes who might experience unwanted side effects.
"We need to do more research and understand how we can use it," she says. "Like which people, which type of patients benefit from which type of mushroom — because that itself is a whole science."
Narayanan and her colleagues also surveyed 2,349 studies examining the relationship between medicinal mushrooms and cancer, but only 39 were robust enough to be included in their 2023 analysis. Of that subset, "31 studies showed beneficial effects of the mushrooms, resulting in improved quality of life, reduced [side effect] profiles of different chemotherapeutic drugs, improved anti-inflammatory and anti-metastatic effects, and improved [disease-free survival] as well as [overall survival] in a few trials," according to the report.
Six studies didn't reveal any advantage and two highlighted worse outcomes. Overall, the analysis was unable to make clear conclusions about "the complex biological effects of mushrooms on the immune system in cancer."
The bottom line
In Narayanan's estimation, there's not yet enough evidence to support routine clinical use in cancer treatment.
And Langer recommends considering a few nutrition basics before introducing a supplement for gut health or cognition. "Take a closer look at what you're eating, how you're eating, when you're eating," she advises, "and see if there's any tweaks that you need to make."
Maybe it's possible to eat more fiber or protein, reduce consumption of alcohol or sugar-sweetened beverages, skip fewer meals, or eat out less often, she says.
"There's so many things that people can potentially improve on," Langer says, "before adding something else that's promised to be this panacea for everything that ails you."

Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.
Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid’s 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.
But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next.
“We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess,” said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. “However, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle.”
Following up
The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida. On Wednesday, ESA released Hera’s first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos. The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as big as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across.
Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there’s no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren’t sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, currently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth.
“I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid,” said Patrick Michel, Hera’s principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. “In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen.”
Hera found Didymos, the larger of the two asteroids, spinning on its axis just as DART observed on final approach in 2022. Dimorphos is no longer so stable.
“As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit,” says Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist.
The Hera spacecraft will fly closer to Didymos and Dimorphos over the next six months to obtain more detailed observations. Hera will release two small sub-satellites to attempt landings on Dimorphos and collect data on the asteroid’s composition, internal structure, and mass.
Scientists will use this information to reconstruct the dynamics of DART’s impact four years ago and better understand how a future deflection mission might move an asteroid off a trajectory that actually threatens Earth. Near-Earth asteroids come in many shapes and sizes, with different densities and makeups, so knowledge of Dimorphos’s physical properties will anchor predictive computer models teaching scientists how best to deflect all types of asteroids.
“Once we understand, we have a breakthrough, which really solves planetary defense,” Michel said in an interview with Ars.
What a mess
In its initial reconnaissance this month, Hera spotted hundreds of boulders surrounding the double asteroid. This was not entirely unexpected. A picture taken by the Hubble Space Telescope shortly after DART’s impact showed a cloud of material streaming behind Didymos and Dimorphos, but scientists were astonished by the extent of the debris swarm in Hera’s first images.
“As we approached Didymos and Dimorphos, we quickly realized the asteroids were not alone,” said Naomi Murdoch, planetary scientist at the Institut Supérieur de l’Aéronautique et de l’Espace in Toulouse, France. “In fact, they had a lot of company.”
An image released by ESA on Wednesday combines 11 long exposure frames from Hera’s hyperspectral camera. Image processors on the ground digitally removed the relatively bright Didymos and Dimorphos to reveal a panoply of dimmer streaks and dots, each of which is a rock fragment ranging in size from a football to a washing machine, Murdoch said.
“Hera came to visit two asteroids, and we found hundreds of companions,” Murdoch said.
One obvious explanation for the boulders is they were thrown off Dimorphos when DART slammed into it. But scientists cautioned they need more information before they can say that with surety. Hera is the first space mission to undertake a sustained study of an asteroid with its own moon. The debris around the two asteroids might be relics from the creation of Dimorphos some time in the ancient past.

SoftBank Investment Advisers’ Narendra Rathi is stepping down from his role as investment director in the company by the end of this year, sources told Inc42. ET reported the development first. As per the report, Rathi intends to launch a public markets fund that will bet on India becoming a significant participant in the AI infrastructure build-out. Rathi’s new fund will focus on industrial companies, including smaller, lesser-known listed firms that could benefit from the growing number of data centres in India, the report said. Inc42 has reached out to Rathi for comments on the exit. The story will be updated based on his response. As per his LinkedIn profile, Rathi joined SoftBank in April 2019 as an investment associate and has served the company under various roles for close to eight years. In 2022, while SoftBank’s India head Sumer Juneja was elevated to oversee investments in Europe, Middle-East and Africa (EMEA) markets, Rathi along with Sarthak Misra were assigned the duty of assisting Juneja. Prior to this, he worked with Morgan Stanley for more than five years as an analyst and associate. He has also been previously associated with companies like Nomura Services India and i3 consulting. SoftBank is one of the major foreign investors in the country and has so far deployed nearly $16 Bn in Indian startups. Having funded nearly a fifth of India’s 100+ unicorns, SoftBank has previously backed the likes of Flipkart, OYO, Delhivery, OfBusiness, FirstCry and Meesho. In the past few months, SoftBank has diluted its stake in listed companies like Delhivery, Lenskart, Meesho and Ola Electric. SoftBank swung to the red and posted a net loss of nearly $7 Bn in Q2 FY26 against a profit of $15.9 Bn in the year ago period. The investment firm also reported $14.1 Bn in net sales in the quarter under review, up 15.6% from $12.2 Bn in Q2 FY25. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that there has been a rise in exits at VC firms in this month, where Nexus VP’s partner Anup Gupta is stepping away from his role, while Fireside Ventures’ cofounder Vinay Singh and principal Prayag Mohanty also resigned from their positions.

In a first, Tamil Nadu govt approves 15-day paternity leave for govt staff
The Tamil Nadu government had received requests from male government employees seeking the introduction of paternity leave.
Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay announced the introduction of paternity leave for male employees working in the state government for the first time.
The male government staff may avail 15 days paternity leave and they may either go on leave 15 days prior to child birth or within six months following the birth of the child, the government said in the official release on Thursday.
The move comes after the government received requests from male government employees seeking the introduction of paternity leave. The female government employees in Tamil Nadu are currently entitled to 365 days of maternity leave.
In August, the state government had announced that it would extend the maternity leave window from 12 weeks to 365 days for its women employees having their third child.
In 2011, the original 90-day maternity leave window was increased to six months, which was further boosted to nine months in 2016, and extended to one year (365 days) in July 2021 by the respective state governments at the time, led by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK).
ALSO READ: Tamil Nadu governor asks CM Vijay to explain why temple lamp wasn’t lit at SC-ordered site
The 365-day benefit is applicable to regular women employees with less than two surviving children as per the standard eligibility framework, news agency PTI reported, citing a government source.
However, as per the directives of the Supreme Court and subsequent state amendments, women employed by the state government with two or more surviving children are entitled to 12 weeks of maternity leave with full pay.

Dubai-headquartered experience management company XEBO.ai has raised $10.5 Mn (around ₹97.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round from Emirates Growth Fund (EGF), the UAE’s flagship growth equity investor. EGF is the sole investor in the round, although the startup is in discussions with other investors who could join in the coming months, cofounder and CEO Yash Sultania told Inc42. XEBO.ai will allocate 30-40% of the proceeds for product development to expand its voice-of-customer (VoC) offerings through voice analytics, digital analytics and agentic AI capabilities. Around 30% of the capital will go towards strengthening its presence in existing markets, including the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), Africa, Asia Pacific and India. The remainder will fund its expansion into new geographies, with North America a key focus. "We are a product company, and around 30-40% of the investment will go towards product development. We want to add more products to our portfolio, particularly around voice analytics, digital analytics and agentic AI," Sultania said. The startup also plans to step up its go-to-market efforts across existing markets while building its presence in North America. Cofounder Anand Nigam has relocated to the US to lead the expansion. Founded in 2017, XEBO.ai operates an experience management platform that helps enterprises collect and analyse feedback. Its offerings span customer experience, employee experience, market research, social listening and customer journey mapping. The startup was previously known as Survey2Connect before rebranding to XEBO.ai in late 2023. Its products help enterprises collect and analyse customer and employee feedback through surveys, voice-of-customer (VoC) analytics, customer journey mapping and social listening tools. XEBO.ai said it serves more than 350 enterprises across over 10 industries, including banking, aviation, telecommunications, insurance, retail, healthcare and the public sector. Its clientele includes HSBC Middle East, Emirates Airlines, Starbucks, H&M, Dubai Properties and the Abu Dhabi government. In India, its clients include Tata AIG, Mahindra Group and others. Around 200 of its clients are based in the Middle East, while more than 50 are in Europe and North America. The remaining clients are spread across Africa, India and Singapore, Sultania said. The startup has also integrated its platform with enterprise and digital experience tools such as Salesforce, enabling businesses to consolidate customer feedback from multiple channels. XEBO.ai follows an annual subscription model, with contracts starting at $10,000 and going up to $200,000, depending on enterprise requirements. It competes with global experience management platforms such as Qualtrics and Medallia. The startup employs more than 100 people, around 80% of whom are based in India. Its Indian operations, which include an office in Noida, are largely focused on product development and engineering. While XEBO.ai has built much of its business in the Middle East, it plans to strengthen its go-to-market (GTM) operations in India. The startup is also looking to expand its presence in North America, with cofounder Anand Nigam relocating to the US to lead the expansion. “We are looking to reach $100 Mn in ARR over the next four to five years. We are targeting accelerated growth in 2027 and 2028, and may raise another round of funding, potentially a Series B, in the next two years to support that growth,” Sultania told Inc42.

Meta declined a suggestion from the UK’s financial regulator last week that they joint-test Muse using their sandbox, according to the watchdog’s head of innovation Colin Payne. It comes as regulators across the UK, including the competition and data watchdogs, warned Meta it needs to ensure its AI products comply with UK consumer protection laws.
“It’s another force of attack, agents hitting the streets, most of them coming from the US,” Payne, of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), said Tuesday in a panel hosted by AI firm Whitespace. “We’ve got a number of entrants into the market. We want to see what they’re going to be doing in the market. I think it’s just reasonable,” he later explained to WIRED. Payne told WIRED the FCA had been hoping the organizations could work together to investigate what interactions might look like between the tool, marketed as a personal assistant, and a normal customer.
His organization has been experimenting with other firms as many, including Amazon, roll out AI shopping assistants, and other agentic tools in the UK.
The FCA especially wants to understand how payments will be made by agents—as multiple British retailers, including grocers Sainsbury’s, Marks & Spencer, and Ocado, department store Debenhams Group, and electronics seller Currys said they’d been working with Meta to smooth Muse’s access to their sites. Payne is concerned about potential unintended consequences of prompts, especially when a user has a low level of understanding of how the AI product works. “If an agent is acting autonomously, we want to make sure it’s in the interest of the consumer,” he says.
Payne did note the testing would have taken time to set up. “Normally you have a long period of time speaking to a firm and then you plan it over a period of weeks or months,” he explained, but Meta only made the FCA aware of its plans last month.
“We’ve engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue to do so,” Meta Spokesperson Matthew Pollard tells WIRED.
More than 10 million users have set up Muse in North America since it was launched in September. British watchdogs say they will be monitoring Muse’s rollout closely as they are bracing for significant uptake on their side of the pond, too, given that many Brits already use Meta’s other products, like Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp. “If it’s going to be equally popular in the UK, we need to be able to see what it’s going to do,” Payne says.
The ICO stressed the importance of users understanding and being able to control how Muse uses their personal data. The Competition and Markets Authority has already made Meta adapt its terms and conditions for UK consumers to say Meta must exercise “reasonable skill and care/professional diligence” when providing Muse, the EU and UK terms say, with the document acknowledging that outputs may still be inaccurate and actions may not be completed as intended.
“If we have concerns, we will not hesitate to act to protect UK consumers,” the CMA said in a statement.

A donation of 121 kg of gold ornaments to Lord Venkateswara at the Tirumala temple has brought attention to Chennai-based entrepreneur Vardhaman Jain. The offering, made on November 26, 2026, is among the major individual contributions reported in the history of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD). Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and his wife, Nara Bhuvaneswari, were present when Jain presented the gold ornaments at Tirumala. The value of the donation has been estimated differently across reports, with figures ranging from ₹150 crore to ₹206 crore. Vardhaman Jain is a Chennai-based entrepreneur known for his work in healthcare technology, business process outsourcing (BPO) and automation. He is the founder and former vice-chairman of Access Healthcare, a company that provides technology-enabled services to the healthcare industry, The Times of India reported. Jain studied Statistics at Loyola College in Chennai before moving to the US to pursue a master's degree in Computer Science from the University of Texas at Austin. His professional expertise includes healthcare technology, medical coding, image processing and robotic process automation (RPA). He also holds several patents related to image processing and medical coding, according to reports. Before establishing his entrepreneurial ventures, Jain held senior corporate positions. The ornaments are expected to be used during daily rituals and special occasions. Reports said the deity would be adorned with the new ornaments on November 27. The 121 kg gold offering is not Jain's first contribution to the Tirumala temple. He has reportedly supported several TTD initiatives since 2019. Mumbai Police issues LOCs against CJP's Saurav Das, Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka over Dadar protest last month
The circulars were issued over the FIR registered against Dipke, Das, Ranka, as well as other CJP members and their supporters on October 3 after the protest.
Mumbai Police has issued look-out circulars against Cockroach Janta Party leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, seven weeks after the organisation's protest in Shivaji Park on October 2.
According to Mumbai Police officials, the circulars were issued over an FIR registered against Dipke, Das, Ranka, as well as other CJP members and their supporters on October 3 for allegedly gathering illegally and sloganeering in Dadar.
The police had denied permission to the CJP’s representative Ajinkya Shinde for organising the protest on Gandhi Jayanti at Shivaji Park, saying they were not empowered to grant permission for any gathering at Shivaji Park.
Deep Dive
An LoC is an alert sent to Indian immigration checkpoints at international airports, seaports, and land borders to track or stop the person named from entering or leaving the country.

The LoC against CJP spokesperson Saurav Das came to light earlier on Thursday after the Centre informed the Delhi High Court about it, stating that it had been done at the request of the Maharashtra Police. Das had moved the HC on Monday (November 23), alleging that he was stopped from travelling to London to deliver a lecture at Oxford University. The CJP had condemned the LoC against Das, saying the outfit spokesperson had not been informed about this when he was stopped at the airport, PTI reported. There was no immediate reaction from the CJP on the LoCs against Dipke and Ranka.
Mumbai Police's FIR against CJP leaders, supporters
The Shivaji Park police had registered a case against Abhijeet Dipke, Pranav Ahire, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde, Saurabh Das, Afreen Nawaz, Saumya Korde, Ankit Bharadwaj, Vijay Malangi and Yogesh Ingle over the protest at Shivaji Park last month. The FIR also mentioned 400 CJP supporters, HT reported earlier.
“We have registered a case against the organisers of CJP protests on October 2 at Shivaji Park. The case has been registered under sections 189 (unlawful assembly) and 223 (disobedience to a public servant’s lawful order) of the Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and section 37 (power to prohibit certain acts for prevention of disorder) and 135 (disobeying or breaking official orders issued by the police) of the Maharashtra Police Act,” a police personnel from the Shivaji Park Police Station had said.
The cops had denied permission for CJP's October 2 protest citing a judgment of the Bombay High Court in PIL 116/2009 dated January 4, 2013, and a subsequent order of the Maharashtra government dated January 20, 2016. The HC order had restricted the use of Shivaji Park for purposes other than sports. Police had also said that the organisers had not submitted the required BMC permission for using the ground.

In a separate development this morning, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre, submitted before Justice Amit Mahajan that an LoC had been opened against him.
The development came days after Saurav Das claimed he was stopped from flying to London.
Senior advocate Akhil Sibal, who was representing Das, told the court that he had not been informed about the LoC and sought details of the circular from the Centre. Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to weather
- Published
Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday because of severe weather.
Preparations to hold the iconic holiday celebration, known for its massive balloons that float among the city's skyscrapers, had already begun when the forecast for heavy rain and strong winds on Thursday led to the delay.
The last time the parade was suspended was during World War Two, but it has never been postponed due to weather. In 1971, Macy's decided to ground the balloons, which often feature beloved characters from pop culture, because of weather.
A powerful coastal storm is set to affect the New York area in coming days.
The potent nor'easter storm is expected to make it too windy and dangerous for the iconic balloons to fly.
Macy's had expected to put 100 inflatables into the sky to mark its 100th parade and feature 10 new balloons, including one depicting the animated dog Bluey wearing a crown and another showing a Minion character riding a banana like a horse.
"While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants and spectators is, and always will be, our top priority," said Will Cross, the parade's executive producer, during a news conference on Wednesday with city officials.
Cross also said the giant balloons would be deflated on Wednesday night and stored at a facility in neighbouring New Jersey until they were reinflated for the parade on Saturday.
Macy's confirmed the new parade date and updated a countdown clock on its website to reflect the Saturday schedule. Meanwhile, broadcaster NBC has said it will show the 2025 parade on Thursday.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who will not attend the parade on Saturday because of a scheduled surgery, said at the news conference that "you have to plan for every possibility" and confirmed that "extreme weather has forced" officials to make the change.
"We know that this is an inconvenience for many who come to visit our city. This decision, however, was made with safety being paramount," he said. "We want to ensure that we're delivering a parade that's not only incredible and spectacular, but one also that doesn't come at the expense of anyone's safety."
Mamdani also said that there would be an expanded police presence along the parade route on Saturday and that there were "no known specific or credible threats to the parade at this time".
Cross added that Macy's is working through what costs it could cover as a result of the delay and said the company is in contact with bands, performers and others who travelled to the city for the parade.
During some past parades, strong winds and inclement weather have led to the tearing and deflation of the balloons as well as collisions with lampposts that caused injuries.
The US National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning, valid from 10:00 local time (15:00 GMT) on Thursday until 01:00 (06:00 GMT) on Friday with gusts potentially reaching 60mph (97km/h) - although the very strongest winds are likely to occur after the parade was due to end.
Heavy rain and coastal flooding will pose additional hazards across the eastern US as the storm sweeps through, while some inland parts could also see snow, BBC Weather reports.
The governor of the neighbouring state of New Jersey on Wednesday declared a state of emergency across the state's 21 counties, beginning at 18:00 local time (23:00 GMT).
Governor Mikie Sherrill's office said the powerful coastal storm is expected to bring damaging winds, heavy rainfall, and severe tidal flooding through Friday, with coastal and bayside communities facing the greatest risk. Sherrill urged residents to stay off the roads as much as possible once the storm arrives.
Originally called the Macy's Christmas Parade, the celebration, which also features live performers, debuted in 1924 as a way to boost holiday sales. It was founded by Macy's employees and their families.
From 1942 to 1944 New York went without the parade as the US directed materials like rubber and helium toward the country's war effort.
The 2.5mi (4km) procession route begins at Macy's Herald Square flagship store and concludes in Manhattan's Upper West Side, with performers and spectators lining the streets to greet Santa Claus and ring in the holiday season.
Country artist Megan Moroney and Grammy nominee Teddy Swims were slated to perform at the flagship store, but it is unclear whether they, along with the dozens of celebrities and float performers on the roster, would be returning on Saturday.

Many social media users have shared a 20-second video of a woman on a bus repeatedly moving closer to the man in front of her. According to the social media claims, the woman was trying to record a fake molestation video.
An X account, MenToo (@MenTooSave), shared the video claiming that the woman in the video was leaning on the man, trying to record a fake molestation video just for views. Noting that such false narrative can put an innocent man’s life and reputation at risk, the post asks, “When will society stop treating every man as guilty by default?”
She filmed herself deliberately pressing her breast against a man’s hand while he visibly tried to create distance and protect himself.
If true, this wasn’t an accident. It was a calculated attempt to manufacture a molestation clip — just for views.
One video. One false narrative. And an innocent man’s life, reputation, and freedom put at risk for content.
This is not empowerment. This is weaponizing accusations. When will society stop treating every man as guilty by default?
Innocent until proven guilty — even when the camera is rolling.
#FalseAccusations #DueProcess #MenToo #JusticeForAll
— MenToo (@MenTooSave) November 19, 2026
Men’s rights activist Barkha Trehan shared the same video on her Instagram account (@barkhatrehan16) on November 20. She also claimed the woman was trying to manufacture a molestation video for views, and the incident was from Patna, Bihar.
Social activist Deepika Narayan Bhardwaj (@DeepikaBhardwaj) also shared the video on X claiming the woman was deliberately sticking to the man so that she could “cry molestation”.
Fact Check
A close examination of the video shows that there is a release announcement poster of a film, ‘Janak’ at the end of the video. Below is a screenshot of the last frame of the viral video:
We then searched for the trailer of the movie, ‘Janak’, and found it on the YouTube channel of Marathi Cineyug, where it had been uploaded on October 14, 2026. The trailer contains the visual that is now viral. The same two people, the same background, clothing and movements can be seen at the 0:49-0:50-second mark in the trailer.
In the process, we also found behind-the-scene photos related to the movie shared on Instagram by Anushka Pimputkar, the woman in the viral clip. In one of the photos, she is seen with Avinash Narkar, the actor who is standing next to her in the viral video.
To sum up, the viral video does not show a real incident of a woman trying to record a fake molestation clip on a bus. It is a scene from the trailer of the Marathi film, ‘Janak’. Social media claims presenting the footage as real are false.

Chennai: In a landmark decision aimed at promoting shared parental responsibilities and strengthening family support, the Tamil Nadu Government has introduced 15 days of paternity leave for married male government employees for the first time.
An official release on Thursday said, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had announced the measure intended to enable fathers to support their wives during childbirth and actively participate in the care of newborn babies.
The release said, the government received requests from employees seeking the introduction of paternity leave for male government staff, on the lines of the 365 days of maternity leave already available to female government employees.
The government recognised that childbirth is a crucial period for both the mother and the child, during which the mother requires physical and emotional support. The father's involvement in newborn care is equally important, the release stated.
The newly introduced provision grants 15 days of paternity leave to married male government employees to be with their wives during the maternity period.
The leave can be availed either 15 days before the expected date of childbirth or within six months from the date of the child's birth.
The initiative is expected to encourage fathers to share family responsibilities, provide essential support to mothers and play a more active role in child-raising.

Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials could undermine decades of medical progress and make even common infections increasingly difficult to treat, a senior health ministry official said on Wednesday, calling for collective action to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
Addressing the national observance of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026 virtually, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava described AMR as one of the most serious public health challenges and stressed the need for a coordinated "One Health" approach to tackle it.
This year's theme is "One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now".
She said medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse.
Srivastava highlighted the interconnectedness of human and animal health, plant and food systems and the environment, noting that improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance.
She said the government has accorded high priority to containing AMR, with the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025-2029, providing a framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action.
The health ministry's National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation, she said.
Srivastava urged healthcare professionals to prescribe antibiotics only when clinically indicated and in accordance with treatment guidelines. She also asked pharmacists to ensure appropriate dispensing against valid prescriptions and counsel patients on their correct use.
She also advised people against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines, stressing that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza.
More than half of antimicrobial sales in India take place without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate, participants at the event noted.
They called for scaling up public awareness campaigns, preventing self-prescription, ensuring proper disposal of antibiotics and expired medicines, and displaying legal warnings at drug shops against the sale of antimicrobials without prescriptions.
Participants also stressed the need to curb production of substandard and spurious medicines, promote appropriate antibiotic use in veterinary medicine, particularly for food-producing animals, and maintain quality standards in healthcare facilities to prevent infections.
The event was attended by senior officials from the National Health Systems Resource Centre, Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, Department of Animal Husbandry, Indian Medical Association and All India Association of Druggists and Chemists, besides officials from states and Union territories.
World AMR Awareness Week is observed from November 18 to 24 every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and promote best practices among the public, policymakers and One Health stakeholders.

Vote for the first BBC Men's Footballer of the Year
- Published
Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.
Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.
The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.
The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.
Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.
"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.
"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner."
The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.
The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).
Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.
Jude Bellingham
Age: 23 Country: England
Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield
Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.
In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.
That meant he joined exalted company as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.
Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.
The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.
Harry Kane
Age: 33 Country: England
Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward
In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.
His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.
Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.
Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.
Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.
Kylian Mbappe
Age: 27 Country: France
Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward
Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.
The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.
Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.
It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.
Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.
He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.
Rodri
Age: 30 Country: Spain
Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield
Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.
By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.
His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.
Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.
His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.
Lamine Yamal
Age: 19 Country: Spain
Club: Barcelona Position: Forward
Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.
Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.
For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.
At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.
He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.
