Quick Answer
You can upscale low-resolution photos for free using offline AI tools. Use Upscayl on Mac and Windows, Upscal on iPhone, or Offline AI Image Upscaler on Android. These apps enhance image resolution up to 4x without uploading your photos to the cloud, keeping them private.
If there is one area where AI has truly revolutionized, apart from writing and coding, it is image upscaling. Whether it’s your old photo taken on a Sony Cyber-shot or one that’s completely distorted, you can give it to AI and you can get a clean, high-resolution version without changing its original form.
Not just your old photos, you can also upscale any standard photo taken on modern phones to the highest resolution possible.
However, one downside of using AI to upscale images, especially if you care about privacy, is that your images need to be uploaded to the cloud for any AI provider, processed there, and then sent back to your smartphone.
Although those images won’t be public, some companies use them to train their AI models. This is the reason why many users, even we, think twice before uploading sensitive photos to AI models for upscaling
Fortunately, tools like Upscayl let the AI model run locally on your device and upscale images to the highest possible resolution without your data leaving your device. Although it has specific hardware requirements, most modern PCs and smartphones support it, and it’s faster too.
It also supports batch processing, where you can upscale multiple images at once. The quality is pretty good too. In this guide, I will show you how to set up Upscayl, a local image upscaler on your Mac, Windows, Android, and iPhone.
Table of Contents
How to Upscale Low-Resolution Photos Locally for Free
Please note that the original Upscayl is only available on desktop platforms like Windows, Mac, and Linux; there are also free apps that use similar technology and work well. I will cover everything in this guide together and help you set up a free image upscaler locally on your device. This guide is designed for beginners, so every step is comprehensive and detailed.
You don’t need much setup to upscale images locally. Since everything comes in one package, the process is very straightforward. You can download the upscaler app; it installs the upscaler model locally and includes a beginner-friendly interface, making it even easier for first-time users.
Below are the steps for each device.
How to upscale photos on a Mac with Upscayl
Step 1: Open Safari or any browser, visit upscayl.org in the address bar, and press Return. On the page, click on the Download button at the top right
Step 2: Now, on the download page, you can see download options for various platforms, including macOS. However, do not click on the macOS button. It opens the Mac App Store, where Upscayl is a paid app. The same app is available for free from Upscayl’s own website.
Step 3: Tap on the alternative download option below and select the DMG version of the app
Step 4: Once downloaded, install the app on your Mac
Step 5: Open the app and complete the onboarding steps. They’re straightforward and easy to follow.
Step 6: Now using Upscayl is easy. In the sidebar, under Step 1, tap Select Image, or drag and drop the image into the right pane.
Step 7: Next, once the image is uploaded, under Step 2, choose an AI model. Upscayl Standard is the best choice for most images. You can also select a different model based on your preference.
Step 8: Now set Image Scale to 4x. This setting makes the image width and height four times larger, so a 480 by 320 photo becomes 1920 by 1280 pixels. You can also drag the slider to change it.
Step 9: Next, under Step 3, you can set where Upscayl saves the new upscaled image. To save it in a preferred location, click Set output folder and choose a folder.
Step 10: Finally, under Step 4, click Upscayl. Depending on your settings and your hardware, it can take a couple of seconds to a minute to upscale images.
Step 11: Once it is done, you can compare the changes. Drag the slider in the middle of the picture to compare the original (left) with the upscaled version (right). The upscaled image will be saved in the folder you set in step 9, or next to your original image file on your Mac.
How to upscale photos on Windows with Upscayl
Next, let’s see how you can upscale images on Windows using Upscayl. The process is very similar to the Mac.
Step 1: Open Microsoft Edge or any browser, go to upscayl.org, and click Download in the top-right corner of the header.
Step 2: Now, on the download page, click the Windows button to start downloading (about 250 MB)
Step 3: Once downloaded, click the file to open it and go through the setup process. If Windows prompts you to allow this app from an unknown publisher, click Yes to start installing.
Step 4: Now select the installation folder; I recommend you keep the suggested installation folder and click Install.
Step 5: Finally, once installed, click Finish to complete the installation on your Windows.
Step 6: Now open the app and go through the setup process. It is very straightforward and easy to follow.
Step 7: Using Upscayl is easy; in Step 1, select an image. If you want to upscale multiple images, turn on the toggle that says ” Batch upscale above Step 1
Step 8: Select the image you want to upscale and tap on Open
Step 9: Now select the upscale model. The Upscayl Standard is best for most photos. Tap it and change it based on your preference. You can also increase the image scale to 4x. By default, it is 4x.
Step 10: Now, in step three, select the desired folder where you want to store the upscaled images, or keep the default, which stores the upscaled version right next to the original file, and tap the Upscayl button to upscale your images
How to upscale photos on iPhone with Upscayl
Upscayl.org is not available for mobile phones. However, free apps let you upscale images locally on your device. Some apps also offer an optional paid plan, but most features are free. Here are the two best upscaling apps.
Step 1: Download the Upscal Enhance Video and Image app on iPhone. Use this link.
Step 2: Once the app is installed, open the app and switch over to the image option
Step 3: Now you can select images from Photos or Files. In this case, I’m choosing the image from my files.
Step 4: The app shows your photo’s current resolution and how much you can upgrade it. In my case, my 480 by 320 photo can be upscaled to 1920 by 1280. Next, tap the settings bar just above Start upscaling. It shows the current model, scale, and format. You can tap the settings icon to customize the model, Upscaling methods, and more.
Step 5: Once you’ve made your changes, tap the Start Upscaling button and wait for the image to upscale. Once complete, you will see the completed status; tap Save to Photos to save the upscaled images to your Photos app.
How to upscale photos on Android with Offline AI Image Upscaler
Similar to iPhone, you can download the Offline AI Upscaler app by Bytesweavers to upscale photos locally on your Android
Step 1: Open the Play Store and download the Offline AI Image Upscaler app by Bytesweavers on your Android phone. You can use this link.
Step 2: Now open the app and tap on Choose photo, then select the image you want to upscale
Step 3: The app shows your photo and the resolution it will make. In my case, it’s 1920 by 1280. To edit the model, you can find the model settings below the photo. The default model is set to Photo AI, which is recommended. However, you can also choose a different model based on your needs.
Step 4: Once you’ve customized it, click Enhance Photo, and that’s it. The app will enhance your photo for a few minutes and when it’s done, drag the slider on the photo to compare the original with the enhanced version. Once you’re done, you can save the photo in different formats.
Give Your Old Photos a New Life With AI
This is how to set up an offline image AI upscaler on Windows, Mac, Android, and iPhone. This setup works completely offline, and many of these methods also support batch processing to upscale your images.
However, for local AI image models, Upscayl is currently the best option. However, it is not as good as any online model. Although it reduces pixelation, it adds softness; if the original image is too distorted and has fewer details, it can soften the image. In most cases with decent images, though, the upscaled version works well. But again, it all depends upon the quality of the original image.
Also remember that upscaling an image multiple times doesn’t improve its quality. Only the first output is the highest quality you can get. I hope you find this detailed and comprehensive guide helpful. If you have any issues setting up the local AI image upscaler on your device, let me know in the comments, and I will be happy to help.

The story so far
The quest for beauty and the enduring appeal for fair and blemishfree skin goes back to ages and across cultures. However, in recent years, this has been landing people in hospitals with serious health issues, as it happened in the case of the 17-year-old girl from Areekode in Malappuram district in Kerala.
Persuaded by many social influencers who raved about a face cream which gave them fair, blemishfree skin, she had also been using the same for over a year. The product with the brand name F-TUNES - claimed to contain turmeric and other “natural ingredients” and cited Dubai as the place of manufacture. She was hospitalised after she developed severe symptoms like fainting spells, swelling on legs and fall in blood pressure and was diagnosed with Membranous nephropathy, a condition wherein the immune system gets dysregulated, triggering nephrotic syndrome (heavy loss of protein through urine). Doctors traced her condition to the heavy mercury content in the face cream she was using. Lab analysis of a sample of the skin lightning cream obtained from the patient revealed that the product contained 12,500 ppm of mercury, way over the legal limit of 1 ppm
After prolonged treatment, the girl is now recovering. The police and drug regulatory authorities have begun a crackdown on the dubious cosmetic products in the market . The Health Minister has also threatened action against social influencers who are peddling dubious cosmetics online

Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests
Updated - November 21, 2026 01:40 pm IST - Kozhikode
As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. (file image)
| Photo Credit: K. Ragesh
People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.
As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

Model-actor Kapil Khadiwala alleged that Indore Police personnel demanded money from his production team during a web series shoot in the city, claiming that the crew was harassed enough to abandon the shoot and return to Mumbai. The police have said they were “examining” the allegations but warned of action if the claims were false.
In a video posted on Instagram, Khadiwala, originally from Indore, tagged the Indore Police with the caption “Shame on Indore Police”, alleging that personnel repeatedly demanded money from his production team and misbehaved with women crew members.
The actor also alleged that obtaining permission for the shoot itself was a cumbersome process, and that the police took two to four days to grant permission and asked several questions “as if the production team was involved in criminal activity”.
View this post on Instagram
“Whether it is the Commissioner’s office, the ACP’s office or the TI (police station in-charge), first, they take two, three, even four days to give permission. And they ask so many questions, as if someone is coming to commit a theft,” he said in the video.
The allegations
In his video post, Khadiwala said that despite obtaining permission, the crew encountered resistance while shooting at a cafe in the Kanadia area. According to him, police personnel arrived at the location around 11-11.30 pm and questioned the team about continuing the shoot.
“When the permission was granted, we were shooting…The police came there at around 11-11.30 pm. They asked, ‘Why are you shooting? Do you have permission for today?’ I told them, ‘Sir, we have permission. We are shooting. People have come from outside, please let us work.’ They started asking why so many people were standing there and said that we could not shoot,” he alleged.
The actor further alleged that police personnel indirectly sought money from the production team and that there were repeated direct demands for money.
“They were preparing to demand a bribe, indirectly asking for money. They directly asked our production people several times how much money they wanted. They said we could not shoot at night. We were then taken to the site, where they were asking for money. They harassed us so much that the shoot had to be stopped. The entire unit stopped shooting midway and went back to Mumbai,” he claimed.
Khadiwala said he felt embarrassed about having brought the production team to Indore and that the crew was now considering shooting in another city.
“I feel so sad and ashamed that I brought these people here. They are taking a break and planning to shoot in some other city. This is a very shameful thing for everyone, that Indore Police behaves in this manner. I had thought of doing something good,” he said.
He also criticised the conduct of senior police officials, alleging that he had been unable to meet the Commissioner of Police.
“I tried to meet the Indore Commissioner. Sir, they have more attitude than Salman Khan. Are they public servants or kings of some country? I don’t understand why this is happening,” he said.
Alleging that police personnel had behaved rudely with women on the set, he added, “Girls were shooting there. Your constables and whoever that person with two stars behaved so badly that they went back.”
Police response
Indore Commissioner of Police Santosh Kumar Singh said the police were examining the allegations and would take action if any officer was found to have violated the rules. However, he also warned that legal action could be initiated against the actor if the allegations were found to have been made “without verifying facts and with the intention of damaging the police’s image”.
“A video has come to our notice in which a person has made certain claims, saying that he was acting in accordance with the conditions of the permission but the police stopped him. All aspects of the matter are being examined. We have social media monitoring cells in every zone and in the Crime Branch, and every such post is taken seriously,” Singh said.
“If there has been any mistake on the part of a police officer or any police personnel, action will be taken as per the rules. But if someone has deliberately not presented the facts correctly with the intention of damaging the image of the police, action will be taken under the applicable legal provisions,” he said.
Asked whether the police would take action if the actor was found to have deliberately damaged its image, Singh said the matter was being examined and that the action would depend on the facts established during the inquiry.
“Any allegation of police misconduct will be examined and, if a mistake is found on the part of the police, action will be taken against the police personnel concerned. But if this person has deliberately made claims without facts and without verifying them, there are appropriate preventive orders and legal provisions under which action can be taken,” Singh added.
Responding to the allegations, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Rajesh Dandotiya said the police had taken cognisance of the actor’s social media post and recorded his statement. However, Dandotiya said Khadiwala told investigators he was not present at the location when the alleged incident took place and that no police personnel had misbehaved with him or demanded money from him.
“The video was identified by the social media monitoring cell. Kanadia Police also identified it and issued a notice seeking the facts and evidence available with him. He was called to record his statement,” Dandotiya said.
According to Dandotiya, Khadiwala said the incident had not happened to him personally. He had allegedly been informed about it by his production manager, Prakash Tripathi, over the phone.
“He told us in his statement that no one misbehaved with him, and nobody demanded money from him. He said he was not even present there. The production manager, Prakash Tripathi, had called him and informed him about it around 12 or 12.30 am. He had left the location at around 11.30 pm,” Dandotiya said.
Dandotiya said the production team had sought permission to shoot between 5 am and 11 pm from November 14 to 20. He said police permissions were subject to established protocols and shooting beyond 11 pm was not permitted under the approval granted to the production team.
“The station in-charge also recommended permission for the same timings in his letter. On the basis of that recommendation, the ACP issued the permission,” he said, adding that the police had now summoned production manager Tripathi to record his statement and would examine the claims before deciding on further legal action.

Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water.
The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23. Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died.
Deaths and transmission
On November 23, Pennsylvania’s health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death, an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child. New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby. On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4.
The virus isn’t slowing down. Measles is the most contagious virus known; it can linger in the air for up to two hours. Up to 90 percent of people who are not immune will fall ill after an exposure. People are considered immune if they’ve been vaccinated or previously infected. With slipping vaccination rates nationwide, the number of susceptible people is only growing.
To keep measles from getting a foothold in a community, vaccination rates need to be 95 percent or higher. According to the latest data, only 92.4 percent of US kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Only 10 states have MMR vaccination rates at or above the 95 percent threshold. But even in those states, there are pockets and communities that are undervaccinated.

Although Amanda Seyfried‘s buzzy new role was a well-kept secret, discretion was maintained with no thanks to her.
The Oscar-nominated actress admitted that although she “was only involved for like a year” in You Can See Everything, she “told a lot of people” about her surprise appearance in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s critically acclaimed documentary about Elizabeth Holmes.
“I’m the most indiscreet person I’ve ever met in my life,” she said on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. “How the hell did I manage to keep it under wraps? I told a lot of people. But I guess I could trust them all.”
Seyfried added, “I mean, I did. I told a lot of people. I mean, one person tweeted something and Nathan was like, ‘What’s this?’ And I was like, ‘I don’t know.’
Watch on Deadline
In You Can See Everything, disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invites Fielder into her and husband Billy Evans’ home to document everything in the month leading up to the start of her 11-year prison sentence on fraud charges.
After portraying Holmes in Hulu’s The Dropout (2022), Seyfried agreed to appear in the documentary, reprising her performance as Holmes in reenactments of moments Fielder was unable to get on camera.
With Seyfried’s appearance revealed during the doc’s surprise September premiere at Telluride, A24 has been building Oscar buzz for the actress, which would be the first time a documentary re-enactor has been nominated in an acting category.

Storms are disrupting Thanksgiving travel, with more severe weather expected to hit the East Coast on Thursday.
More than 6,500 flights within, into, or out of the US were delayed on Wednesday, and about 160 were canceled, according to FlightAware. As of about 1:30 a.m. ET Thursday, roughly 120 flights had been delayed and 300 canceled.
The National Weather Service wrote in a Wednesday report that the East Coast can expect "major coastal flooding, beach erosion, strong wind gusts, and heavy rainfall" during Thanksgiving.
Scattered power outages and tree damage are also likely, it added. A map from the weather service showed winter, gale, coastal flood, and wind warnings along the country's eastern coast.
NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani wrote in a Wednesday X post that New Yorkers should expect severe weather on Thursday, including winds up to 60 miles per hour.
He said that, to protect New Yorkers, the city, along with Macy's and the local police department, had decided to postpone the 100th Annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday. This is the first time in history that the iconic parade has been rescheduled.
"The worst of the storm is expected to hit on Thanksgiving Day in the afternoon through the late evening," he added in his X post. He provided a list of steps New Yorkers should take to protect themselves ahead of the storm, such as staying indoors, moving cars away from coastal areas to higher ground, and budgeting extra time for travel.
The Transportation Security Administration said in a Saturday X post that it expects to screen nearly 17.6 million passengers nationwide between November 24 and November 30, including more than 3 million on Sunday, November 29. It recommended that travelers arrive early for their flights.
The Federal Aviation Administration wrote in a Wednesday X post that gusty winds may slow flights at LaGuardia Airport, Newark Liberty Airport, JFK, and San Francisco International Airport that day. It added that thunderstorms may cause delays at Miami International Airport and Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport.
Business Insider has put together a handy guide for passengers whose flights are canceled or delayed this weekend.

20 నవంబర్ 2026న ముంబైలోని కుర్లా వెస్ట్‌లో, ఫీనిక్స్ మార్కెట్‌సిటీ మాల్ సమీపంలోని ప్రమోద్ మహాజన్ గార్డెన్‌లో ఒక యువ జంటపై కొంతమంది మైనర్లు దాడి చేశారు. ఒక గుంపు ఆ జంటను చుట్టుముట్టి, అసభ్యంగా ప్రవర్తిస్తూ,  దాడి చేసారు. ఈ దాడికి సంబంధించిన వీడియో వైరల్ కావడంతో పోలీసులు ఎనిమిది మంది మైనర్లపై కేసు నమోదు చేశారు. వారిని 4 డిసెంబర్ 2026 వరకు జువైనల్ కరెక్షనల్ హోమ్‌కు పంపించారు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ).
ఈ ఘటన నేపథ్యంలో, పోలీసులు కొంతమంది వ్యక్తులను ఊరేగిస్తున్నట్లు చూపించే వీడియో ఒకటి సోషల్ మీడియాలో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) వైరల్ అవుతోంది. ముంబైలో యువ జంటపై దాడి చేసిన వారిని పోలీసులు ఇలా ఊరేగిస్తున్నారని ఈ వీడియోను షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు. ఈ పోస్టులో చేసిన వాదనలో నిజమెంత ఉందో ఇప్పుడు పరిశీలిద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: ముంబైలోని కుర్లా వెస్ట్‌లో యువ జంటపై దాడి చేసిన నిందితులను ముంబై పోలీసులు రోడ్డు పై ఊరేగిస్తున్నట్లు ఈ వీడియో చూపిస్తోంది.
ఫాక్ట్: ఈ వైరల్ వీడియోలో గుజరాత్‌లోని సూరత్‌లో 18 ఏళ్ల సంతోష్ మోరే హత్య కేసులో అరెస్టైన నిందితులను చూపిస్తున్నారు. ఈ హత్య కేసుకు సంబంధించి సూరత్ పోలీసులు నిందితులను ఊరేగించారు. ముంబైలో యువ జంటపై దాడి చేసిన వారిని కాదు. కాబట్టి, ఈ పోస్టులో చేసిన వాదన తప్పు.
వైరల్ వీడియోలోని కీ ఫ్రేమ్‌లతో రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, 2026 నవంబర్ 14న Gujarat Live అనే ఇన్‌స్టాగ్రామ్ ఖాతాలో అప్‌లోడ్ చేసిన వీడియో లభించింది. ఈ వీడియో ముంబైలోని కుర్లా ఘటనకు ముందే అప్‌లోడ్ చేయబడింది. ఆ వీడియోలో ఉన్న వివరణలో, సూరత్‌కు చెందిన యువకుడు సంతోష్ మోరే హత్య కేసులో అరెస్టైన నిందితులను చూపిస్తున్నట్లు పేర్కొన్నారు.
దీనిపై కీవర్డ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, వైరల్ వీడియోలోని దృశ్యాలతో కూడిన పలు మీడియా రిపోర్టులు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) లభించాయి. ఈ రిపోర్టుల ప్రకారం, 8 నవంబర్ 2026న సూరత్‌లోని రసూలాబాద్ ప్రాంతంలో 18 ఏళ్ల సంతోష్ మోరేను కత్తితో పొడిచి హత్య చేసినట్లు ఆరోపణలు ఉన్నాయి. ప్రేమ వ్యవహారానికి సంబంధించిన వివాదం, గత కక్షల కారణంగా ఈ హత్య జరిగినట్లు సమాచారం. ఈ కేసులో జావేద్ అలియాస్ నవాబ్ షేక్, హన్సరాజ్ కుష్వాహా, షకీబ్ మానియార్, షాహిద్ షేక్, పీయూష్ సాహూలను నిందితులుగా గుర్తించారు.
2026 నవంబర్ 12న సూరత్ పోలీసులు తమ X ఖాతాలో అప్‌లోడ్ చేసిన వీడియోలో కూడా ఇలాంటి దృశ్యాలే కనిపించాయి. ఈ వీడియోలో అదే నిందితులను పోలీసులు ఊరేగించడం చూడవచ్చు. ఈ వీడియోకు జత చేసిన వివరణలో, ఖటోదరా పోలీస్ స్టేషన్ పరిధిలోని ఆజాద్ నగర్‌లో ఒక యువకుడి హత్య కేసులో నిందితులను ఖటోదరా పోలీసులు అరెస్టు చేసి, చట్టం గురించి వారికి గుణపాఠం చెప్పారని పేర్కొన్నారు.
చివరిగా, హత్య కేసులో నిందితులను సూరత్ పోలీసులు ఊరేగిస్తున్న వీడియోను, ముంబైలో యువ జంటపై దాడి చేసిన ఘటనకు సంబంధించినదిగా షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు.

Suresh Mittal is 87. According to Uttar Pradesh’s latest draft electoral roll, his father, Vansh Mittal, is 23. Both are registered at house number 869 in booth 111 of the Dholana constituency in Hapur. The same roll lists Vansh as the son of Ajay, a 56-year-old in the same house.
Suresh is not an exception. Alt News found 1,10,875 voters in the Special Summary Revision (SSR) draft roll whose father or mother, registered in the same booth and the same house, is recorded as the same age as them or younger. The draft was published on November 17.
A Year of Revisions: First SIR, Now SSR
The draft comes at the end of a long year for UP’s voter list. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the rolls began on October 27, 2025 and ended with the final roll on April 10, 2026. In those 166 days the state’s electorate shrank from 15.44 crore to 13.39 crore.
As per the process of SIR, every voter was supposed to be issued an enumeration form, which was supposed to be collected by booth-level officers (BLOs). The Election Commission’s software then allegedly went through the data looking for what it called logical discrepancies. One of these was a parent less than 15 years older than the voter. About 2.22 crore voters in UP were sent notices for such discrepancies, and the Commission says hearings were completed on all of them.
On October 15, six months after the SIR’s final roll, the Election Commission ordered a Special Summary Revision (SSR) in 17 states and Union territories, including UP. The SSR draft roll, which merges the SIR roll with all supplementary lists, has 13.58 crore electors. Claims and objections can be filed till December 16, and the final roll is due on January 4, 2027.
What We Found and How
The SSR draft rolls are machine readable. We took every voter whose entry names a father or a mother, and looked in the same booth for a voter with that name living in the same house. If that ‘parent’ turned out to be the same age as the voter, or younger, we flagged the entry.
We found 1,10,875 such cases spread across all 75 districts and 403 constituencies.
In 35,523 of these cases, parent and child are the same age. In the other 75,352, the parent is younger, and in 6,860 of them by 20 years or more.
Some of the cases are shown below for representation:
What did SIR Actually Achieve?
The SIR was designed to weed out exactly this kind of error. It had enumeration forms, BLO visits, software flags and hearings. A parent who is younger than their own child is perhaps the most basic inconsistency a voter list can have. This raises a larger question: if a process this elaborate left the most basic errors untouched, what did the SIR actually achieve?
Moreover, spotting these anomalous entries is no rocket science. Each one is a contradiction between two lines of the same booth’s roll, often on the same page: An 87-year-old whose father is 23, a 123-year-old woman whose mother is 45, two women who are each other’s mother. A simple check on the roll itself would have thrown them up. Either no such check was run, or nobody acted on what it found.
As of now, all 1,10,875 are in the draft, and the window for corrections closes on December 16.
The district-wise and constituency-wise count of such cases is given below. Kushinagar district has the most cases (3,646), and Fazilnagar has the most for a single assembly constituency (711).
Skip to PDF content
In a related report published on November 21, Alt News showed several glaring anomalies that the final SIR list for Uttar Pradesh had, including at least 230 voters listed multiple times across 69 booths, missing addresses, unexplained name and gender changes, and suspicious deletions. The report can be read here.

A latte is rich and milky heaven. A cappuccino is the cloud that heaven rests on. The best latte machines and the best automatic espresso machines are the ones that can give you this richness consistently, easily, and deliciously. Home espresso machines, like the classic devices in our guide to the Best Espresso Machines, often have a reputation for being intimidating. But they don't have to be.
Some machines make it easy and keep you from having to drive to the coffee shop. The automatic espresso machines in this guide can make a perfect frothy cappuccino accessible with the press of a single button, or maybe a couple of buttons. Our top high-end superautomatic espresso machine, the De'Longhi Rivelia (7/10, WIRED Recommends), is a paragon of easy-peasy, frothy, pleasing cappuccinos and flat whites. The new Ninja Cafe Luxe Pro (see here on Amazon) seems determined to produce every kind of coffee in existence.
Most of the machines on this list also come with grinders, but our guide to The Best Coffee Grinders may also be helpful. For more WIRED coffee coverage, check out our guides to The Best Coffee Subscriptions, The Best Drip Coffee Machines, The Best Milk Frothers, and The Best Cold Brew Makers, or look for our recent coffee gear reviews.
Updated November 2026: We’ve added information on WIRED UK’s blind taste test of popular fully automatic bean-to-cup machines and ensured up-to-date links and prices.
Best Automatic Latte and Cappuccino Maker
A sophisticated bean-to-cup machine from Italian coffee titan De'Longhi, the Rivelia (7/10, WIRED Recommends) immediately ranks among the most modern, impressive, user-friendly, and capable superautomatic espresso machines I’ve encountered—the sort that has you dump a half-bag of beans into a hopper and will grind, brew, then froth up milk for a flat white, amid 18 options on espresso, latte, cappuccino, and iced-coffee drink options.
Pretty much everything operates via an easy touchscreen, including bean guidance that lets you optimize the machine for each bean. The milk frother works at the press of a button and makes actual microfoam—and the foam’s density can be adjusted to make a frothier cappuccino or dense flat white. It’s so easy I let my parents test-drive it, and they fell in love with it within a day. If you’ve got multiple people using the machine, you can save multiple profiles and your favorite custom drinks. So Dad can have his basic “coffee” that’s actually a European-style café crema, and Mom can have her ridiculously large 16-ounce travel-mug latte. (Yes, these are their drinks.)
What's better, the Rivelia has two swappable bean hoppers, so it’s easy to swap between caff and decaf, or between light and dark roasts. Honestly, this is the bean-to-cup espresso machine that fully sold me on the idea of automatic coffee machines like this one. Though note: Fully automatic espresso machines like the Rivelia grind a little coarser, in order to make espresso less finicky and less difficult. This leads to a smoother but less nuanced profile than espresso shots you’d find in a café. But if you're a milk lover, the absolute ease with which the Rivelia froths a cappuccino will likely balance this out. The cold espresso is also a pleasant option when mixed with milk or vodka.
Best Semiautomatic Latte Machine With Cold Foam
A lot of machines can make you a cloudy, clumpy, big-bubble cappuccino without much hassle. But it's that well-integrated microfoam, the silkiness, that feels like an actual luxury—elevates a good foamed milk from the merely milky latte to silly morning ecstasy.
There's a lot to like about Ninja's flagship entry into the espresso market: in particular, dosing by weight and an easy bean guidance function that actually helps in dialing in a bean. Quite simply, this machine offers real-deal, unpressurized portafilter espresso without the fussiness. But what I especially like about this Ninja is the milk. Some superautomatic machines have tube-filled, plasticky milk systems that are annoying to clean. Some never get a fine froth. This Ninja Luxe Cafe Pro is the best of each world, a steam wand and stainless steel steamer cup with a spinning whisk at its bottom that simulates the whirlpool created by a skilled barista. Whether cold foam or hot foam, Ninja's Luxe Cafe series offers truly excellent foam for your morning cup.
Now, for this: It is not a superautomatic machine like the Rivelia, though it’s among the easiest portafilter machines I've ever used. The conical burr grinder is built in, it doses accurately, the tamper handle is easy, and bean guidance will tell you what to do without much fuss. Mostly, you just need to transfer the portafilter from one spot on the machine to another.
Note that for a lower price, the Ninja Luxe Cafe Premier (described below) offers the same great milk froth, but you lose the automatic tamper and a hot water spout. For me, the Pro is the pick for a more pleasant morning and greater versatility. Note that while the massive drip tray does hold a lot of water, it’s a bit of a production to empty and replace, and that while it also purports to be a drip coffee maker, it’s nothing to write your mother about.
Best Budget Latte Machine
This Mr. Coffee machine was once our top pick for lattes. Why? Because it sits so nicely at a comfortable intersection where ease of use meets automation and affordability. This is about the lowest-priced machine you can ever expect to find with automatic milk frothing at the press of a single button, with options for latte foam or cappuccino froth. Just load fine-ground coffee into the portafilter, tamp it down, and twist it on. The machine will mix up a cappuccino or a latte macchiato at the press of a button.
This machine has a forgiving (but not overly intense or nuanced) pressurized portafilter, which means it will work with almost any “espresso-grind” coffee from your local café or the grocery store. Just note you’ll still get a better shot of espresso if you buy a grinder and use fresh beans from a good specialty roaster. But all in all, this is about the easiest $200 latte machine we know. Like, the hardest thing about it is that the milk canister can be removed and stored in the fridge, and you have to clean it out once a week.
Best Budget Superautomatic Espresso Machine
The Cafe Affetto is one of the few fully automatic machines that WIRED has enjoyed in this price range. The Affetto features a built-in steaming wand, produces 20 bars of pump pressure to ensure your espresso is fully extracted, and is a slick little machine. It’s very slim and fits comfortably on a small apartment countertop without having to rearrange everything. Because coffee production is automated, you just need to fill the water tank and put whole beans in the hopper, and you’re good to go. You can brew one or two shots with just the press of a button, and there’s a programmable button to create your favorite drinks (like an Americano with just the right amount of water).
The milk frother does a lot of the work on its own. Just pour some of your favorite milk into the frothing pitcher, submerge the wand, and hit the steam button. If you’re new to frothing milk, you don't even need to move the pitcher to produce a creamy and consistent microfoam. WIRED reviewer Jaina Grey tested the frother with dairy milk, oat milk, and soy milk, and found it produced soft and creamy café-grade froth each time. Just make sure it’s topped up with water and beans and that you clean out the spent grounds container regularly, and it works like a dream.
Best Semiautomatic Espresso Machine
The Breville Oracle Jet (8/10, WIRED Recommends) is my favorite of the two dozen or so new espresso machines I’ve tried so far this year. It’s the one I recommend as my top pick in WIRED’s guide to the Best Espresso Machines, over other estimable contenders from Breville that include the Barista Touch ($1,000) and the Barista Pro ($850). And it’s the one that best mixes full-flavored, nuanced espresso with the ease of machine-guided, touchscreen operation. It’s versatile, it’s powerful, its PID controller means the brew temperature is quite stable, and it makes absolutely lovely cups—espresso that’s denser and more intensely aromatic than the coffee made by any other machine on this list, whether in bringing out the fruity berry notes in an anaerobic light roast or the dark chocolate of a roasty Italian.
In the finicky, often difficult world of classic home espresso machines, the Oracle Jet is a paragon of simplicity and machine-guided brewing: It’s a miracle that one can so easily pull such delicious and nuanced shots that remain so sensitive to the character of each bean. But that sensitivity still makes the Oracle Jet a little more finicky than other machines on this list. And while the automatic milk frothing is quite good, it’s not as failsafe as our favorites here. (I still like steaming milk manually on the Breville, versus using the auto-froth.)
Which is to say that as a latte machine, this Breville is all about the espresso. If you want espresso that will distill the beauteous character of fresh-roasted beans but still don't want to try overly hard—on a machine whose intuitive touchscreen tutorial will guide you to lovely flat whites and capps? This is your huckleberry.
Best Pod Latte and Cappuccino Machine
For those who’d rather not fuss with beans at all but still want a lovely milk-frothed latte and cappuccino in the morning, there is this clever two-piece setup from Nespresso—with “espresso” on one machine via Vertuo coffee pods and an Aeroccino milk frother that’s whisper-quiet and will whip you up some milk foam in a minute. The espresso that comes from pods is not quite espresso, of course, but WIRED reviewer Louryn Strampe loved it best of all pod espresso machines, with excellent body and mouthfeel and especially ease. The Vertuo Pop+ will also make a drip-coffee-style mug.
But this frother bundle generally offers you a good bargain on an all-in-one system, and the Aeroccino is in the upper echelon of milk frothers WIRED has tested. (Note, however, you'll have to plug in each machine separately.) This said, if you want the ease of pod espresso but are fussy about your milk, you may want to grab a stand-alone Vertuo Pop+ ($129) and the excellent Dreo Baristamaker ($100). Do this when a good sale is running, and you might cobble this together at a similar price to the Aeroccino bundle.
The Aeroccino was easy to use—pour in your milk of choice and press the button. it will heat and froth your milk automatically—it takes about a minute, and it’s whisper-quiet. Every Nespresso capsule I’ve tried has featured a thick layer of crema, and having whipped, thick milk on top of it made my average cup of coffee a more elevated experience.
Best Handheld Milk Frother
Sometimes making a whole latte or cappuccino using an automated machine can be a time suck. Not to mention, sometimes all you really want is frothy milk. That’s where milk frothers come in. These machines beat air into milk, or milk substitutes, to get that nice creamy froth. Former WIRED Reviewer Jaina Grey loved this handheld from Subminimal, a highly specialized immersion blender that makes properly textured, creamy, light, airy, wonderful milk. One screen makes fine-textured milk. One makes “ultra-fine.” Note that Subminimal has also added a milk frothing pitcher called the Nanofoamer Pro ($159) that costs a bit more, but is currently sitting prettily atop our guide to the Best Milk Frothers.
Other Automated Latte and Cappuccino Machines We Liked
This streamlined machine from relative newcomer Terra Kaffe is a pleasant surprise, given the complexity of Terra Kaffe's first machine, the superautomatic TK-02 (see below), which bristled with features and doohickeys. The Demi is perhaps the dead-simplest fully automatic espresso machine I've yet encountered that still makes good coffee. If you don't want to customize your shot, there's just a dial and a button: espresso, lungo, Americano, drip, hot water, bye!
You can click into submenus and edit these to a nerd's content, both by volume and strength. You can adjust among five grinder settings as well—a low but relatively typical number of settings for automatic machines that already grind coarser than espresso machines with portafilters. You may need to futz with grind and dose strength to get good results with light roast, especially on espresso, but with a good medium roast, the Terra Kaffe offers a very smooth ride. Honestly, this is the machine I'd put in a front room for customers to use if I owned a small business. Super easy, no fuss, good for multiple types of people—and the reservoir is big enough at 1.4 liters that you won't be refilling the water all day.
But note that this is actually not a latte machine: It's only half of one. There's no milk frother. Luckily, the world is full of good milk frothing jugs these days, and we especially recommend the Subminimal Nanofoamer Pro ($159), WIRED's favorite milk frother.
Ninja has a habit of taking high-falutin', pro-level, or commercial equipment—whether soft-serve ice cream machines or slushie machines—and finding a way to make it easy, accessible, fun, and probably viral on TikTok. WIRED contributing reviewer Tyler Shane was skeptical about Ninja's first foray into the latte and cappuccino world with the Luxe Cafe Premier (7/10, WIRED Recommends), especially since the machine also promised cold brew and even traditional drip coffee. But she came away impressed.
This Ninja is not a superautomatic machine like our top automated pick, the Rivelia. It's what the industry likes to call “semiautomatic.” Semiautomatic espresso machines offer a built-in grinder and automatic milk frother but still use a non-pressurized portafilter that will pull a classic espresso shot with full nuance and aromatics. In our espresso maker guide, we recommend the ever-reliable and terrific Breville Barista Express ($700) as WIRED's favorite accessibly priced semiautomatic. But this Ninja is the machine I'd probably give to a beginner, a new college grad, or anyone whose first priority is ease and great automatically foamed milk
The drip coffee is meh, granted. But more than perhaps any semiautomatic machine in its price range, the Ninja Cafe Luxe Premier is geared to absolute ease and versatility—with an intuitive digital user interface that helps you along. Depending on your chosen drink, the Ninja Luxe will recommend the appropriate grind size on its display screen and help you dial it in. (This may take a couple of tries.) Milk frothing is easy, and the automatic milk frothing is shockingly good. Plus, you can froth cold foam, for silly cold-foam drinks. See what I mean? Ninja is fun. That said, we ended up preferring the Luxe Cafe Pro ($750), which costs a little more but adds a welcome auto-tamper and hot water spout.
This superautomatic espresso machine is one of the few coffee machines made by German auto and appliance behemoth Bosch. It is both highly sophisticated and a bit of an odd duck—capable of making an unholy variety of espresso drinks downloaded via firmware. The milk system is especially interesting, and for some, it may be the biggest selling point. On the base model, the milk system is basically a tube you attach to the side of the brew head. You can stick the other end of the tube in any container, and it'll steam whatever milk you've got directly into your cup before adding the espresso. This is great for families who use multiple milks. It's also great for not wasting milk.
The espresso is similar to superautomatics from De'Longhi, which is to say it's a smoother, more rounded, but less nuanced take on espresso that's great for milk drinks. But the “drip” is also interesting. The Bosch 800 “slow brew” coffee—while it does not have the clarity or brightness of drip coffee— is perhaps my favorite drip coffee from an espresso machine, round and roasty and lovely. It extracts only the smooth, chocolate end of the coffee spectrum. I haven't tested the pH, but it seems quite low in acidity. It's nice.
But here are the caveats: Coffee cup height clearance can be an issue on milk drinks, the pump is a bit louder than some, it's slow to boot up, and some parts feel a bit flimsy or plasticky for a machine in this price range. Also, if you do want an attached milk carafe, it's hundreds of dollars more, depending on current deals.
The delta between home espresso machines and the commercial workhorses used by busy third-wave shops is still thousands of dollars, but that hasn’t stopped both beloved brands and scrappy upstarts from infiltrating the space with more approachable units. Skip the junk and level up to the Casabrews 5700PRO (7/10, WIRED Review), which offers an unfussy take on the art of homemade espresso drinks.
Instead of bewildering noobs with a million settings and onboard tutorials, this 12 x 11 x 16-inch tank of a machine keeps it simple with easily accessible controls for things like temperature and dose volume for extraction, and run time for the onboard grinder. It's a single-boiler machine, not a dual boiler, which means you can’t froth your latte milk at the same time as pulling a shot, but the texture of the frothed milk is perfectly malleable and up to snuff for a basic leaf or rosetta pattern.
The guide rails that hold the portafilter in place are a bit too close to the output spout of the grinder, and temperature controls that deal in absolute rather than relative values would be welcome improvements. But until Casabrews implements our feedback, this is still a solid unit that’s a great pick for anyone who’s ready to never leave their house for a cappuccino ever again. —Pete Cottell
The superautomatic Terra Kaffe is a pricey hunk of machinery and has its bugs, but considering its ease and customizability, it's worth the price, wrote WIRED contributing reviewer Tyler Shane last year. She praised the device's convenience, its ease, the front-facing water filter, waste tray, and milk carafe, and its excellent app (available for iOs and Android) that offers easy controls and the ability to warm up your machine from your bed or the bathroom.
Drinks like latte macchiatos, drips, and iced coffee can all be adjusted to your tastes, and a milk frothing dial allows you to adjust the milk’s texture from foamy to silky. For those who love true, real, drip coffee, that's the biggest selling point for the Terra Kaffe over our top automated picks, the De'Longhi Rivelia and the Ninja Cafe Luxe Premier: The TK-02 offers it. The drip coffee is also good enough that Shane cleared her Chemex pour-over carafe from her counter.
De’Longhi’s Magnifica Start is a no-nonsense superautomatic with a conical burr grinder, four preset recipes at the push of a button, and the ability to brew a smooth and potent espresso, wrote WIRED contributing reviewer Tyler Shane. As with other high-end De'Longhi devices of the moment, the milk frother is truly impressive, offering seriously luxurious frothed milk. Milk-based recipes at the touch of a button are a latte macchiato and a cappuccino, while espresso and Americanos are the espresso-based options. There’s a slot for ground beans and a hopper for whole beans. Figuring out grind size takes a little trial and error, Shane noted, and it's not an overly quiet machine. But the Start is compact and efficient, and priced far lower than our favorite De'Longhi automatic, the Rivelia. This makes the Magnifica Start a solid investment.
Questions and Answers
The key here is automation. We wanted to test machines that make you a cup of coffee with a single touch, or as close to that as possible. So the products on this list are all of the automatic and semiautomatic variety. You fill ’em up and they do all the hard work—or most of it, anyway. Nothing here doesn't have a milk frother that does the work by itself.
Setup and cleanup were especially important, as was durability. The entire point of a device like this is to save time and energy and/or produce a drink of higher quality than can be made without it, so we didn’t recommend any products that didn’t produce tasty espresso and save time.
In May 2026, WIRED’s UK team gathered four fully automatic machines—the Terra Kaffe TK-02 (above), Philips’ Café Aromis 8000 Series, De'Longhi's Eletta Explore, and Jura E8—and made both lattes and espressos for local industry experts to judge. You can read the results and watch the resulting video here. The Reviews team is currently testing the winner of that challenge, Philips Café Aromis 8000, to see how it compares against the top picks in this guide.
Even if you're not making espresso, the first and best thing you can do to dramatically improve your morning coffee is to buy locally roasted beans. Plug your city or region and “locally roasted coffee beans” into Google and you will be glad you did. The reason that your locally roasted coffee will taste worlds better than anything you'd buy from a major coffee roaster (like Starbucks, Illy, or Gevalia) is simple: Good coffee starts to lose flavor the moment it's roasted. Get it fresh and you're giving yourself a much better chance at high-quality espresso.
Want some help finding the best roasters? For some of our favorite mail-order brands, with beans often roasted the same day or week they're placed in the mail, check out our roundup of the Best Coffee Subscription Services.
I hate to break it to you, but pre-ground coffee from a supermarket bag is pretty much always worse. Unless you see a roasting date on the bag, you probably have no idea when the roaster actually roasted it. If the roaster is a French or Italian brand, there's a good chance it was months ago. Coffee is best when it's fresh, ideally brewed a week or two after it's roasted. And grinding the beans dramatically increases the rate at which coffee degrades. This doesn't just affect how the coffee tastes. It affects how well the espresso maker will push water through the beans, leading to possible blowouts or bad extraction.
If you haven’t made espresso before and you don't have access to a coffee grinder, we recommend you buy locally roasted beans. Just ask your local coffee roaster for a fine (espresso) grind. We've tried a lot of pre-ground espresso blends from popular companies like Lavazza, Gevalia, and Café Bustelo. They were all very dark and very bitter, partially because they are all either imported or roasted in big batches and shipped all over the world. Pre-ground coffee will always be a little stale, and it's hard to get a good cup from coffee that's started to degrade—which happens fast after you grind it.
Get it ground fresh from a local roaster, and you'll have about a two-week window before you'll notice any difference. Many of the machines recommended here come with a grinder, so whole beans are already the best choice. But our roundup of The Best Coffee Grinders can also provide some guidance here, if you want to get into the grinding game, buy whole beans, and keep your coffee tasting its best.
Look, milk is milk. Anything that contains milk has the potential to get strange over time, and this includes the milk containers and milk frothers on automatic espresso machines. WIRED's previous espresso reviewer, Jaina Grey, was extremely sensitive to this issue—devoting her time to dishwashering, soaping, scrubbing, and otherwise testing the best methods for making sure that milk containers on automatic espresso machines remain sacrosanct environments.
Regular washing is, of course, the first and best recourse. But occasionally, you'll also want to sterilize your milk reservoir and milk frother.
First, hand-wash it with soap and water as usual, and make sure you get a sponge into those corners. Next up, there are a couple of options. The most effective will be a food-grade sanitizer like Star San, or One Step. Essentially, just make a dilution per the instructions on either product, pour that into a spray bottle, give the inside of the milk container a couple of sprays, and let it dry on a drying rack.
The second-best option, the one that uses things you probably have in your house right now, is a mix of distilled white vinegar and plain old tap water. If you have staining or really stubborn smells, you'll want to let it soak. Try adding about one shot glass (1.5 ounces) of distilled white vinegar and fill the container up the rest of the way with warm water. Let it soak for about 30 minutes, then rinse it out till there's no more vinegar smell, and you should be good to go.

World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) for the immediate lifting of the U.S. fuel blockade on Cuba, ‌warning that the measure was putting the lives of children at risk.
“The intensification of fuel restrictions and sanctions is causing direct harm to the Cuban people, especially the most vulnerable,” Mr. Tedros said on ‌a recent visit to Cuba that included tours of several healthcare facilities in ‌Havana.
“It is endangering their lives, including the ‌lives of children.”
During his three-day visit, the official said his organization would contribute $2 million to help strengthen Cuba’s national immunization program and provide essential medical equipment to healthcare facilities.
Like the World Health Organization, ‌the United Nations has also repeatedly warned of a growing humanitarian crisis on the island, calling the U.S. fuel blockade a violation of international ‌law and the human rights of all Cubans.
The Cuban government says U.S. sanctions have led to daily power outages lasting 20 hours or more, critical shortages of medicines and surgical supplies, and a decline in health indicators, such ‌as infant mortality rates.
Washington argues the energy blockade is intended to push for political change on the island, and says that exports of food and medicine are subject to legal exemptions.
Tensions between the two nations have soared since the ‌administration of U.S. President Donald Trump ramped up pressure on Cuba since January, imposing a fuel blockade on the island and stiff sanctions against a swath of Cuban officials and state entities.
An annual non-binding resolution calling for an end to a U.S. embargo on the island ‌has passed in favor of Cuba in the UN General Assembly by wide margins every year since 1992.

The COVID-19 pandemic is having a devastating impact across the world. Efforts to contain the coronavirus are vital to the health of the world’s population, but they are also exposing children to increased risk of violence – including maltreatment, gender-based violence and sexual exploitation.
As leaders of organisations committed to ending violence against children, we come together in solidarity to share our deep concern, call for action and pledge our support to protect children from violence and reduce the impact of COVID-19 on children in every country and community.
A third of the global population is on COVID-19 lockdown, and school closures have impacted more than 1.5 billion children. Movement restrictions, loss of income, isolation, overcrowding and high levels of stress and anxiety are increasing the likelihood that children experience and observe physical, psychological and sexual abuse at home – particularly those children already living in violent or dysfunctional family situations. And while online communities have become central to maintain many children’s learning, support and play, it is also increasing their exposure to cyberbullying, risky online behavior and sexual exploitation.
The situation is aggravated by children’s lack of access to schoolfriends, teachers, social workers and the safe space and services that schools provide. The most vulnerable children – including refugees, migrants, and children who are internally displaced, deprived of liberty, living without parental care, living on the street and in urban slums, with disabilities, and living in conflict-affected areas – are a particular concern. For many, growing economic vulnerability will increase the threat of child labour, child marriage and child trafficking.
We must act now. Together, we call on governments, the international community and leaders in every sector to urgently respond with a united effort to protect children from the heightened risk of violence, exploitation and abuse as part of the broader response to COVID-19.
Governments have a central role to play. They must ensure that COVID-19 prevention and response plans integrate age appropriate and gender sensitive measures to protect all children from violence, neglect and abuse. Child protection services and workers must be designated as essential and resourced accordingly.
Working with and supporting governments, our collective response must include: maintaining essential health and social welfare services, including mental health and psychosocial support; providing child protection case management and emergency alternative care arrangements; ensuring social protection for the most vulnerable children and households; continuing care and protection for children in institutions; and communicating with and engaging parents, caregivers and children themselves with evidence-based information and advice. National helplines, school counsellors and other child-friendly reporting mechanisms enable children in distress to reach out for help, and must be adapted to the challenges of COVID-19.
Given the heightened risks of online harms, technology companies and telecoms providers must do everything they can to keep children safe online. This includes providing access to cost-free child helplines, age-appropriate services and safe e-education platforms - and using their platforms to share child online safety advice. They must also do more to detect and stop harmful activity against children online, including grooming and the creation and distribution of child sexual abuse images and videos.
As global organisations working to end violence against children, we will continue to advocate for and invest in effective child protection solutions. We will collectively develop and share technical resources and guidance for policymakers, practitioners, parents, caregivers and children themselves. And we will support the courageous health, child protection and humanitarian professionals working around the clock to keep children safe during these unprecedented times.
In recent years, the global community has made significant gains in protecting children from violence. We must not allow those gains to be lost during the current turmoil. We must do all we can to keep children safe now. And we must plan ahead together, so that once the immediate health crisis is over, we can get back on track towards the goal of ending all forms of violence, abuse and neglect of children

(Bloomberg) -- Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the Salvadoran man deported to a notorious prison in El Salvador in what US officials called an “administrative error,” said he “can breathe freely” after arriving to Spain.
“Today we celebrate because I not only feel victorious and we won the fight,” Abrego Garcia said at press conference Wednesday. “This time because I’m leaving with my freedom, not like before when they took me out inhumanely.”
Abrego Garcia’s battle was one of several high-profile legal disputes over the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. He was mistakenly deported last year to CECOT, a notorious Salvadoran mega-prison, only to be brought back to face criminal charges after the US Supreme Court ordered the government to facilitate his return to the US.
He arrived in Madrid Wednesday after the 18-month legal battle where the government had sought to deport him to African countries, including Liberia. He had also faced a US human smuggling prosecution until a US judge in May dismissed the charges, concluding the government brought the case in retaliation for his fight against deportation.
“We are going to continue to fight for all the people that are experiencing an injustice,” Abrego Garcia said. “Clearly the government did not decide where my story continues. My family and I decide where my story goes from here.”
In 2019, an immigration court issued an order prohibiting the government from removing him to El Salvador after the court found he faced danger from a gang that had targeted his family.
Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, his American attorney, said Wednesday that Abrego Garcia traveled to Spain under a tourist visa for a “short term” stay. The US government was required by court order to lift “all impediments” that barred Abrego Garcia from leaving the country, including removing him from a no-fly list.
Abrego Garcia, whose wife and son are American citizens, could be eligible to return to the US as a legal permanent resident. But, he will need waivers from the State Department, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio will not grant, Sandoval-Moshenberg said.
“It is going to be up to the next administration to reunite this family as quickly as possible,” he said.
Senator Chris Van Hollen, a Democrat from Maryland who met with Abrego Garcia in the Salvadoran prison last year, said the Trump administration had engaged in a “vendetta” against him.
“Kilmar and his family are relieved that he is now in a place of his choosing, a free man and living with dignity,” Van Hollen said. “I think the message for all of us is that it’s never wrong to stand up for our Constitution. It’s never wrong to stand up for the rule of law.”
Both immigration advocates and the Trump administration said that Abrego Garcia’s departure was a win.
Ama Frimpong, chief of services and legal advocacy at We Are CASA, said rather than being deported, Abrego Garcia made the “choice” in where he went.
“This is what we fight form the freedom to choose how we live with safety and dignity,” she said.
Meanwhile, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued a statement taking credit for Abrego Garcia’s exit. He labeled Abrego Garcia as a “human trafficker” and “MS-13 gang member.”
Abrego Garcia has denied the government’s allegations.

Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 on Friday, November 20, 2026, involving a child who tested positive for measles, the state health department said.
The department said the child was between 0 and 4 years old. It did not disclose additional details, including the child's vaccination status, citing the family's privacy.
Measles can cause serious complications, including pneumonia, brain inflammation, complications during pregnancy and death.
Virginia has reported 220 measles cases so far in 2026, including 40 among children aged 0 to 4 and 75 among those aged 5 to 12, state health department data showed as of November 19. Of those cases, 179 were in unvaccinated individuals, 39 were in people whose vaccination status was unknown and two were in vaccinated individuals.
Virginia health officials have reported increased measles activity driven largely by outbreaks in central region. Buckingham County has reported 127 cases, the highest in the state, while neighbouring Charlotte County has recorded 34 cases.
The death adds to a worsening national measles outbreak that this week cost the United States its measles elimination status after 26 years.
Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit U.S. state, reported an eighth measles-related death and confirmed 1,631 measles cases, as of November 20. Wisconsin has also reported two deaths, while New York state recorded its first measles-associated death, involving a child.
The CDC has confirmed six measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, though it does not specify the states where the deaths were recorded.
A discrepancy between state and federal death tallies arose earlier this year after the CDC, under US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures.
The sharp increase in U.S. measles cases has coincided with declining immunization rates and rising vaccine hesitancy under Kennedy, who has for years spread doubts, without scientific evidence, about the safety of measles vaccines.

China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
BANGKOK — Chinese Communist Party authorities are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, China's anti-corruption watchdog said Tuesday.
The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth.
Chen is under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. The brief announcement by China's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection provided no further details.
A statement released by the Shanghai city government said the Standing Committee of the Shanghai Committee of the CCP "expressed firm support" for the decision to investigate Chen.
The decision sent "a clear and powerful signal that the fight against corruption would continue without pause or retreat," but with "a firm determination to win," the statement said.
The investigation follows sweeping purges under Xi, who has emphasized greater party discipline. The Chinese leader has pursued an anti-corruption campaign for more than a decade, carrying out purges on a scale not seen since Mao Zedong's rule.
"The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign has no limits," Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, said in an emailed statement. "This is the fourth Politburo member to fall, and the fourth sitting member brought down in the current cycle. The pattern is unprecedented."
The recent Politburo purges highlight how much Chinese politics depend on shifting circumstances, with even officials with qualities that Xi apparently valued being vulnerable to removal, said Joseph Torigian, a professor at American University based in Washington.
"On paper," they appear to be "individuals Xi would appreciate," Torigian said, but afterward, "we could easily come up with hypotheses for why he got rid of them."
Other Politburo members purged include Gen. Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission, which oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary.
The post of Shanghai party secretary has traditionally been viewed as a stepping stone to China's top leadership. The country's former President Jiang Zemin, its current premier, Li Qiang, and Xi himself previously held the position.
Chen has served as Shanghai party secretary since 2022. He previously held senior positions in Beijing's municipal government and headed the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

Motorcycle rider who took stunning cricket catch found
- Published
"I told my friend riding the motorcycle to duck his head. I'm going to catch it."
Mehran Khan amazed sports fans around the world this week when he caught a cricket ball while sitting on the back of a moving motorcycle.
Mehran was passing a match in the Swat Premier League in Mingora, Pakistan, when a ball sailed out of the ground towards him, with the passenger reaching out to catch it one-handed.
Speaking to the BBC, he said of the grab, which has gone viral online: "I didn't think I would actually catch it."
Mehran was on his way home from work at the Public Health Engineering Department when he saw the ball being struck.
"I'm a cricket fan," he said. "I play cricket myself and I watch it too. I saw that Abrar Lala was at the crease and then he hit a six.
"I told him [the friend who was driving] to duck his head. I'm going to catch it. Then I caught it.
"I made the effort, but I didn't expect to catch it. I thought it would fall somewhere nearby, but by the grace of God I managed to catch it."
According to Mehran, immediately after the catch the Swat Premier League organisers announced a prize of 10,000 Pakistani rupees (about £27.60) for him, funded by the Pakistan Army.
The Marghazar resident was caught by surprise when the recording of the catch spread so quickly online, saying: "The video went viral overnight. I didn't even know about it."
He expressed his happiness at receiving the award, saying he was grateful to God, and added that he had returned the ball after taking the catch.
"People are saying I was taking the ball away with me, but that's not true. I returned it," he said.
Swat Strikers won the match against GKR Dir by 34 runs, and Mehran urged the organisers to continue holding the tournament every year, describing it as an "excellent competition".
One of the most unusual catches
There have been several remarkable catches by spectators at cricket matches in the past.
In 1987, during a match in Australia, a cameraman casually caught one off former England all-rounder Ian Botham's sixes while holding a cigarette in his mouth.
In 2014, during a New Zealand domestic match, a spectator slid down a slope and completed a one-handed catch.
Last year, in a match between Australia and South Africa, a fan caught a ball with one hand while holding two drink cans in the other.
Mehran's one-handed catch while sitting on a moving motorcycle will join them in cricketing history.

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said it had cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Pune-based Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation for the second time after the firm was found to have manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission, all of which were subsequently declared substandard, misbranded or spurious by government analysts.
The cancellation order, issued on November 23 by the Joint Commissioner (Drugs), Pune Division, directed the firm to immediately cease all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution activities. The FDA has also proposed prosecution against the firm under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
Of the nine drugs tested, two were declared spurious after government analysts found that the claimed active ingredients were absent. Ibucare Plus, a combination of ibuprofen and paracetamol, contained no ibuprofen, while Carevita-M, a multivitamin tablet, was found to contain none of the nine specified ingredients tested.
The remaining drugs failed various quality tests, with several containing significantly lower quantities of active ingredients than claimed on their labels. These included medicines used in the treatment of cardiovascular and digestive disorders.
The FDA said the firm, located in the Additional MIDC area of Jejuri in Pune district, had admitted in its written response that it had not obtained separate product permissions for the nine drugs.
Earlier violations
The firm’s manufacturing licences had previously been cancelled on September 7 after a joint inspection conducted on July 14 and 15 revealed 25 serious deficiencies in Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
The inspection revealed that approximately 13.86 lakh tablets of Caregyl-400 had been manufactured without mandatory batch manufacturing and packing records or test reports. Of these, 5.20 lakh tablets had already been distributed. Laboratory analysis revealed that the sampled batch contained only 32.44% of the claimed metronidazole content.
Several samples of substandard drugs were also collected from the Central Medical Store of Yashwantrao Chavan Memorial (YCM) Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad, following which stocks worth approximately ₹1.72 crore were seized on November 4.
Other irregularities included discrepancies in manufacturing and expiry dates, inadequate laboratory testing procedures, unhygienic manufacturing conditions and improper storage of finished products.
Risk to patients
A show-cause notice was issued to the firm on October 29, following which it submitted a written response on November 3. A personal hearing was conducted on November 23.
The licensing authority rejected the firm’s contention that no patient complaints had been received, observing that the risk of treatment failure arising from spurious and substandard drugs existed even in the absence of complaints.
“Ensuring that citizens have access to safe, quality and efficacious drugs is the foremost responsibility of the Food and Drug Administration. Stringent regulatory and legal action will be taken against any manufacturer who plays with the health of the general public by manufacturing drugs without product permission,” FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said.
