Walmart has asked Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down, three sources aware of the development told Inc42 as the investigations into alleged seller kickbacks widen across the company. The probe, which was initially reported to cover Flipkart's smartphones and luggage and travel accessories (LTA) categories, has now expanded across the group, including fashion ecommerce platform Myntra and travel booking platform Cleartrip, the sources added. According to the three sources, the investigation has unearthed kickbacks across the various companies within the group with some of the top executives allegedly involved in receiving kickbacks from preferential sellers, brands for enhanced visibility and sourcing of materials. One of the sources said that Walmart had earlier asked CFO, Sriram Venkataraman to step down following reports of financial irregularities/ kickbacks at the firm. Notably, Venkataraman announced his exit in March 2026 Additionally, sources said the decision to ask Krishnamurthy to step down is also tied to a delayed IPO timeline for Flipkart and to achieving the ecommerce company's profitability target. “Walmart has been firm that Flipkart must speed up its IPO process and improve profitability, and has appointed consulting firm McKinsey to carry out a pre-assessment of the company’s IPO readiness”, the sources said. Walmart also questioned Flipkart’s expansion into new verticals such as food delivery and microdramas, among other ventures, which it saw as delaying the IPO, they added. All of these factors together led to Walmart asking Krishnamurthy to step down, the sources said. Sources also indicated that the ecommerce major may also see more senior-level exits following the departure of Krishnamurthy from the firm. The ecommerce giant issued a statement confirming Krishnamurthy’s exit, but it did not reveal the reason for the leadership change. Sources added that the parent company decided to make a change after Krishnamurthy’s decade-long stint at the helm. In an official statement on Wednesday, the company did not indicate that this was about the Walmart investigation. Instead, Flipkart said the overall business grew more than fivefold during his tenure. Incidentally, Krishnamurthy’s statement on his exit touched on ethics and integrity, in addition to business growth. “I am proud of the scale of the business we have built, but equally proud of how we have built it. Strong ethics, integrity and high standards of governance have been central to Flipkart’s growth,” Krishnamurthy said in the statement. Flipkart said it will appoint a successor in the coming weeks. Balaji Thiagarajan, currently Flipkart’s chief product and technology officer, will lead the company in the interim, along with the Flipkart board. “Both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan. We are grateful for his leadership, the governance he instilled and his many contributions to the company,” Chris Nicholas, president and CEO of Walmart International, said in a statement. Inc42 has reached out to Flipkart with queries on the probe and the circumstances of Krishnamurthy’s exit. The story will be updated as and when the ecommerce company responds. What Led To The Ouster Sources told Inc42 that the investigation unearthed kickbacks across Flipkart's sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, and design teams, as well as its group companies. Executives allegedly took commissions from sellers to boost their visibility on the platform and compromised the quality of material sourced for Flipkart's private-label business, the sources said. “This has been going on for several years and is largely a compliance issue,” one source said. The wider scope of the probe today compared to 2024 is largely because of a precedent of such allegations at the Flipkart group. Sources said a key member of Myntra's design team quit over similar allegations a few years ago, followed by a similar resignation at Flipkart. The most recent probe was sparked after sellers directly approached Walmart with complaints about being asked to pay a kickback fee for greater visibility on Flipkart. This prompted the parent company to act. Things came to a head in late October 2026, when Walmart launched an investigation following the whistleblower complaints. Reports speculated that Flipkart employees received kickbacks of over INR 150 Cr (about $16 Mn) from vendors; however, the actual amount has not been officially revealed. The allegations pertain to employees offering vendors preferential treatment, including greater visibility on the platform, in return for payments and favours. In the smartphones category, employees allegedly took cuts from vendors as devices moved between businesses, including through Flipkart's B2B operations. However, the extent of the alleged kickbacks and the number of employees involved is not yet clear. This was reportedly Walmart's third such investigation at Flipkart in less than three years. US retail behemoth’s second concern has been a mega listing of Flipkart, which has now missed its deadline for a few years in a row. “Walmart was also concerned about the recent performance of Flipkart during its flagship Big Billions Day Sales and is particularly not happy with the core marketplace business performance,” a company insider told Inc42. In Walmart’s Q3 FY27 earnings call last week, CFO John David Rainey said the sale’s timing created a 100 basis point headwind to Walmart’s top line growth in Q3, and that the Big Billion Days performance “will be reported in International’s fourth quarter results this year”. The ecommerce major had been preparing for a listing for years, and after completing its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026, it was expected to go public in late 2026 or early 2027. It was also exploring a pre-IPO round of about $2.5 Bn. Those plans were put on hold in May, when Walmart reportedly asked Flipkart to pause fundraising and focus on profitability, pushing the IPO to at least 2028. Kalyan Krishnamurthy’s Exit Leaves A Vacuum Krishnamurthy’s exit is the first major leadership change in Flipkart since the acquisition by Walmart in 2018. He joined the company in 2016 from Tiger Global, one of the early investors in Flipkart. Soon after that, he was appointed as Flipkart CEO in January 2017, and then took over as group CEO in 2018 after cofounder Binny Bansal resigned following an investigation into allegations of personal misconduct. As CEO, Krishnamurthy became the face of the company into its second decade, after founders Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal had led the company from 2007 to 2017. And now, as Flipkart enters its third decade, and prepares for a potential IPO in the near future, it will be led by a new CEO and there could be other changes in the offing, given recent headlines around an IPO The CEO’s exit comes at a time when Flipkart is already dealing with a string of senior departures and discontent among former employees over delayed ESOP buybacks, even as other companies have listed and executed buybacks. As reported, more than 1,000 former Flipkart Group employees had earlier approached Walmart's board seeking equal access to stock buybacks offered to current staff. The leadership churn now adds to the uncertainty around Flipkart's IPO plans. Krishnamurthy had said in July that the company had no timeline for going public, while Walmart has reportedly asked Flipkart to hit EBITDA breakeven by the end of March 2027 before pursuing an IPO or a fresh funding round. In FY26, Flipkart's consolidated operating revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 1,45,880 Cr, while its net loss narrowed marginally to INR 8,468 Cr from INR 8,646 Cr in FY25. The consolidated numbers include Myntra and Cleartrip, following Flipkart's redomiciling to India. While the first phase of Flipkart’s journey was defined by its founders, the previous ten years have seen the company branch out into new categories, such as the Cleartrip acquisition, the fintech push, the foray into food delivery, and of course the aggressive investments for its quick commerce app Flipkart Minutes. All this means the incoming CEO will have to lead a Flipkart that’s vastly different from the company that Krishnamurthy inherited. Whoever steps in will have big shoes to fill.

In a powerful explosion that launched gray-white clouds over southeastern Iowa, the Army detonated 68 barrels containing 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of degraded lead azide on Wednesday at about 9 am CT, preventing a spontaneous unmitigated explosion of the crystallized, highly unstable compound.
The detonation occurred at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, a town of fewer than 400 people. Residents within a 5-mile area of the facility were advised to evacuate, while people farther out were told to shelter in place, close windows and doors tightly, turn off fans, and set indoor air systems to recirculate.
Local Iowa outlet KWQC caught the plume from the two earth-covered containers, which were detonated simultaneously. A KWQZ journalist, at a reportedly safe distance from the blast, said on the live broadcast that he could see and then feel the shockwave roll through the crop field in which he was standing. He put a mask on for the rest of the broadcast.
Lead is a neurotoxin that does not break down in the environment and poses significant health risks, particularly to young children and pregnant people.
In the hours leading to the detonation, the Army released maps showing modeled drift and distribution of the plume. They indicated that airborne lead would travel around 100 miles to the southwest of the facility, while dust deposition would cover around 200 square miles in that direction. Researchers and government workers have already collected air and soil samples from the area, which will act as baseline readings for lead levels in the aftermath and fallout of the detonation.

WhatsApp is testing stickers with sound
The feature is now rolling out in public beta.
WhatsApp's latest public beta release adds a new feature that could make chatting with your friends more fun: stickers that play sounds when you tap them. You know how the chat app lets you create your own stickers, even animated ones? Well, it's pretty much the same thing, except you can also add audio. That gives you an easy way to recreate iconic video clips, such as Josh Hutcherson's Whistle edit meme, which has been making the rounds again thanks to the Sunrise on the Reaping movie.
According to WABetaInfo, sound stickers are part of beta update 2.26.41.3 for Android. If you want to try it out, you can apply to become a tester for the chat app through Google Play. To make a sound sticker, open a chat, tap the sticker icon and then tap Create sticker. From there, you can choose a video from your library, which WhatsApp will automatically convert into a sticker.
Now, you'll find the new Sound icon at the top menu. Tap it to open the new Add sound screen. From there, you can keep the video's original audio, record a voice note or any other custom sound you want to use, or choose an audio file saved on your phone. When you're done, you can save the sound sticker and send it to as many people as you want.
Since the feature is experimental, you might not be able to access it right now, even if you're already a beta tester. WhatsApp has yet to announce whether it will roll out to all users in the future.

According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide.
Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft’s target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. “Needless to say, we aren’t here yet,” Henderson wrote.
The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company’s post-incident report, dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident.

The Hindu will conduct a free health webinar on Saturday, November 28, 2026, on the topic ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’. The webinar will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m.
Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs. These disorders can affect different parts of the body, including the joints, skin, nervous system and other organs, and may present with a wide range of symptoms.
The session will explore how autoimmune conditions develop, the role of the immune system, and the common signs and symptoms associated with these disorders. It will also discuss early warning signs, including persistent fatigue, joint pain, muscle weakness and neurological symptoms, and explain when these warrant medical attention.
The discussion will examine the challenges involved in diagnosing autoimmune conditions, the role of clinical evaluation and diagnostic tests, and the treatment options available. The panellists will also discuss long-term disease management, monitoring, and the importance of timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment.
Expert panellists include Aishwarya G., Consultant Rheumatologist and Clinical Immunologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai. The panel will also feature Prabash Prabhakaran, Director and Senior Consultant – Neurology, SIMS Hospital, Vadapalani, Chennai. He will discuss autoimmune conditions affecting the nervous system, the neurological symptoms they can cause, approaches to diagnosis and treatment, and the importance of recognising neurological manifestations.
The session will be moderated by Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu.

England's state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world's largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years.
The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset.
The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians' time.
The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS.
"This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world," Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech's "huge potential" while pledging "proper safeguards" to ensure safety and effectiveness.
"If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery."
The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England.
Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out.
The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel.
The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two.
Recruitment has started at Cambridge University Hospitals, in eastern England, with more of the 30 selected sites opening in the coming months.
Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, with around 55,000 diagnosed every year in the UK.
Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for screening every three years, amounting to around 2.1 million screenings annually. The NHS estimates this helps prevent around 1,300 deaths.
A study published in The Lancet medical journal in January said that AI can improve breast cancer detection through more effective screening while reducing radiologists' workloads.
It analysed nearly 106,000 mammograms performed in Sweden as part of its national breast cancer screening programme -- involving women with a median age of 53 -- from April 2021 to early December 2022.

Players in limbo after NZ netball league collapses

All Parris Mason has known is playing netball. But with a World Cup just nine months away, she and four other New Zealand players have been left in limbo after the collapse of their domestic league.
"There's a high potential I will not be playing netball heading into a World Cup," she told BBC Sport.
While a significant number of her Silver Ferns team-mates play professionally in Australia and England, Mason stayed with her home league.
The 23-year-old defender, who has been a full-time professional for six years, found out her netball fate when the news was leaked to the media.
"It shattered me," she said. "The influx of emotions; is my career over? What do I do next? It was just so much to handle all at once."
Netball New Zealand admitted the way events unfolded publicly was deeply regrettable and has pledged to support the affected players.
"We know this period of uncertainty has been extremely tough for players, coaches, teams and everyone involved in the domestic competition," a statement said.
"Their wellbeing is our priority, and we are working closely with the New Zealand Netball Players' Association to support them."
It comes as the Silver Ferns are on the cusp of becoming the world's number one ranked side, after winning gold at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and beating Australia in the Constellation Cup.
The World Cup will be held in Sydney, Australia, between 25 August and 5 September, with New Zealand looking to win the title for a sixth time.
What happened to the ANZ Premiership?
There had been uncertainty over the future of the ANZ Premiership for a couple years. The league had struggled to secure long-term broadcast deals which impacted the league financially.
In 2026, the league recorded a loss of around $NZ 3.7m (£1.5m). There was an exodus of the country's best players.
Ten of the 12 Silver Ferns who won gold for New Zealand at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow have moved overseas to play - primarily in Australia.
Businesswoman Anna Mowbray and her husband, former All Blacks player Ali Williams, pitched a new private league for 2027, but negotiations fell through just eight weeks after signing a term sheet.
"I don't understand my life without netball," said Mason. "It's been a big part of my identity, and [there is a] mental toll to [being] continually knocked down.
"I think of everything in this whole situation as just completely sad."
Nathan Limm, who has been following the story for the New Zealand Herald said: "The Ferns' success feels a little bit fragile. They get a few injuries, where's the depth underneath if they're not playing domestic netball?
"The communication between Netball NZ and the Players Association, with their investors, with the public, has been so rocky.
"I think there is a real distinct lack of trust between the players and Netball NZ."
When asked whether there are plans for a domestic netball competition next season New Zealand Netball said: "Work on an elite domestic competition for 2027 is well under way. Our goal is a sustainable, professional competition for 2027 and beyond."

Whatever happened to the diamond that went missing in F1 crash?
- Published
Where were you between the hours of 1pm and 3pm on 23 May 2004?
If you were in Monaco, consider yourself a suspect - or at least a witness - in Formula 1's biggest unsolved mystery.
A $300,000 diamond was last seen stuck to the front of an F1 car before it crashed on the first lap of the Grand Prix and it still has not been found 22 years later.
Did someone pick it up? Was it swept up with all the debris? Did it slip down a drain? Was it even a real diamond?
Someone, somewhere, knows something.
The reason why a 1.4 carat diamond was attached to the most delicate part of a car that reaches 200mph in a race was straightforward: publicity.
Jaguar Racing's results on the track had been mediocre at best since becoming an F1 team in 2000 and by 2004 its parent company Ford had decided it would be pulling them out of the sport.
"My job flipped from primarily running the team to primarily selling the team and finding a new owner or they would shut it down," former team principal Tony Purnell tells BBC Sport.
"It was probably the worst year of my life. Particularly because for the first few months I was sworn to secrecy."
His team needed some good PR to divert attention away from performance and improve its appeal.
They had enjoyed a successful promotional weekend in Silverstone the previous season thanks to a tie-up with Terminator 3 and so director of communications Nav Sidhu was looking to recreate the magic with another bit of help from a movie.
"I'd heard on the grapevine, around about the winter of 2003, that they were making Ocean's Twelve and we discovered that they were shooting some of the scenes in Monte Carlo," Sidhu says.
"One thing led to another and before you knew it, we had agreed [a deal] with George Clooney, Brad Pitt and Matt Damon."
Sidhu had arranged with legendary Hollywood producer Jerry Weintraub to have the film's branding and stars take over the team for the Monaco weekend.
The film plot centred on an audacious theft of a diamond-encrusted Faberge egg. Sidhu decided he wanted some sparkle on his cars too at the most glamorous race in the F1 calendar.
Sidhu negotiated with diamond company Steinmetz that the two Jaguar cars would have gems - which would today be worth about $1m in total - attached to them.
What happened next, though, was not part of the script.
While the champagne corks were popping on nearby mega yachts in the principality, the diamonds were being hand-delivered into the garages. There were two that would be mounted on to the car and a larger gem just for the photos.
The diamonds for the cars were encased by steel and fixed to the nose cones. One on experienced driver Mark Webber's car and one on rookie Christian Klien's.
Webber was starting from 11th place in the grid and Klien - in only his sixth race - was starting from 14th. They weren't expected to challenge for the podium, but they were expected to bring the diamonds back.
Monaco's street circuit is demanding, with narrow roads, tight turns and a tunnel.
Overtaking is difficult and crashes are common - as Klien soon found out.
In a chaotic first lap, the Austrian made contact with one of the Jordan cars exiting the Mirabeau corner. This damaged the front of his car - where the diamond was - and led to a slow collision with the barriers at the famous Loews hairpin.
Klien climbed out unhurt but the front of the car was crumpled.
It was not long before Sidhu had the diamond company on the phone asking if they would get their diamond back.
"I can't remember what I answered, but it certainly wasn't 'yes'," he says.
He couldn't even get on to the track to have a look as the race had another 76 laps to go and only then would the car - which had been lifted off the track by a crane and left behind the barriers - return to the garage.
"I was consumed with getting to that spot as quickly as I possibly could," Sidhu says.
"That hour and a half waiting for the race to finish felt like a day and a half, every single lap was just like pulling teeth."
By the time he had the chance to have a look, there was no sign of the diamond.
But there were plenty of theories.
Theory: it was not a real diamond
Sidhu completely denies the rumours of a fake diamond.
"I've learned that any diamond company is not going to go out there, particularly in the public domain, and use fake diamonds because clearly there's a high risk of being caught," he says.
"Had we used a fake diamond in that car and what took place took place, then clearly the embarrassment and the disrepute it would bring Jaguar, and Formula 1 for that matter, was too high risk.
"There's been loads of conspiracy theories about was it a real diamond or was Christian told to crash his car and I think that's what's given the story its life - there's a mystery to this story and that mystery will always breed different theories."
Purnell backs up the legitimacy of the diamond, recalling a conversation he had with the managing director of the team, David Pitchforth.
"David said, 'Tony, it was definitely real because when they came to the office with it, I picked the diamond up, went to the window and scratched the window' because that's how to tell.
"Hearing that from Dave, I'm in no doubt it was the real thing that was put on the car.
"I don't know if one of our mechanics was switched on enough to make a fake, but I don't think so."
Theory: someone pocketed it
"I think somebody probably just picked it up, put it in their pocket and... they're probably smiling and thinking, 'it's in my drawer'," says Purnell.
"I do think also that a fairly large diamond zooming through at 100 miles an hour probably shattered. Somebody's got a little bit, somebody else has got another [little bit].
"Maybe, sadly, just some guy was sweeping up the road or one of those trucks with the brushes and it all went down the sewer.
"It did occur to me that the ultimate thing would be if Clooney, Pitt and Damon had contrived to steal it because it was so in line with Ocean's Eleven. But that was a fantasy too far."
There would have been hundreds, if not thousands, of people in the area because within an hour or so of the end of the race the circuit would have been returned to public roads.
Sidhu is pretty certain about what happened to the diamond: "Someone's picked it up.
"What people tend to do is, believe it or not, pick up bits of tyre rubber, you know, claim that as Michael Schumacher's front tyre rubber or whatever they can find.
"Somebody may have picked it up not having any idea it came off a car.
"There's a lot of diamonds in Monte Carlo. There's a lot of people walking around Monte Carlo with a lot of jewellery and a lot of stones.
"Somebody dropped a diamond in Monte Carlo. Well, they're not going to miss that, are they? Probably not."
Theory: Klien crashed on purpose
Sidhu says the cost of the damage to the car was more than the cost of the diamond, which reports at the time said was uninsured.
And points and a good result in the race were more valuable to the team and individuals than a diamond or the publicity a crash would bring. It was simply not worth crashing on purpose.
"For us, bringing two cars home, ideally in the points, had far bigger commercial benefits to us in terms of constructors' points, broadcast money, and more importantly, trying to retain our sponsors and trying to protect the integrity of the team," Sidhu explains.
Klien drove straight into the barriers right in front of the marshals so would not have had the chance to start looking for a diamond or picking it up even if he had wanted to.
"Christian didn't try and say all the brakes failed or anything like that, he's just said 'I made a rookie mistake'," says Purnell.
"He was a young guy, first time, made a mistake, it happens. Doesn't usually happen with a $300,000 diamond flying into the crowd or wherever it went, but I'm sure Christian wasn't really aware of the diamond.
"No amount of money would have got Christian to do that [crash on purpose]. He wanted to make a success of what he was doing."
While events were unfolding, Purnell had not really been thinking about the diamond.
His main concern that day was that one of his drivers had crashed and the other also did not finish, and that this was not a good look in terms of pleasing current backers or attracting potential buyers.
"When Christian went into the wall and then later Mark retired, my entire thinking was 'Oh God. What am I going to say?' The chairman of HSBC [Jaguar's then sponsors] was there, Sir John Bond. Jackie [Stewart] was there.
"It was all about 'how am I going to explain another bad performance? How am I going to say 'just stick with the plan? We know what we're doing, it will take time' because sponsors don't have time. They want success."
In the end, the missing diamond came to the rescue.
"No-one mentioned Jarno Trulli winning the Grand Prix, no-one asked how the Jaguars did. No-one was interested that Mark Webber's car broke as well. It was, 'where's the diamond?'" says Purnell.
"I remember talking to somebody in Detroit saying, 'fantastic publicity over here, you know we never hear anything about Formula 1 but it's on the newscasts, it's in the papers - fantastic'."
Asked if the diamond mystery had helped the eventual sale of the team to Red Bull six months later, he replies: "I think that helped quite a lot because it buzzed the Jaguar team and showed that huge publicity was possible even if you weren't doing so well."
Red Bull went on to become hugely successful, winning eight drivers' championships and six constructors' championships since joining F1.
"You couldn't design a better PR weekend," says Purnell.
Even if it was not quite how it was planned and there is still the small matter of a missing diamond.

Residents of a village in Odisha's Koraput district protested against the construction of a church-cum-prayer hall allegedly on government land and vandalised the structure, prompting the local administration to form a peace committee to maintain communal harmony in the area, police said on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
The incident occurred at Patraguda village under the Kotpad block, where tribal people objected to the construction of the church, following which a district administration team visited the site and issued a show-cause notice to the man who had built the structure, a senior officer said.

The incident came to light after Durjyadhan Harijan, belonging to the only Christian family in the tribal village, lodged a police complaint on November 21, alleging that a group of locals had vandalised the Beersheba Pentecostal Church.
The villagers were also accused of damaging the cross and parts of the prayer hall, the officer said.
"The villagers alleged that the church was established on government land which was meant for community use and not for one family. The person had failed to produce any land documents to establish his ownership of the site. Kotpad Inspector-In-Charge Runu Majhi said the case was under investigation and no arrest had been made so far.

Maharashtra will soon start issuing property cards called Vertical Property Cards for individual flats. These cards will record details such as an apartment’s area, related rights, and any legal hurdles against it, also serving as a separate record of rights along with the existing land records.
Around seven crore flat owners will be beneficiaries of this card, said Maharashtra Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said, adding that the draft of rules and regulations will be open for suggestions and objections from November 26. Rules will be finalised based on the inputs.
“In rural areas, the 7/12 extract is available for land, and in urban survey areas, the property card (Milkat Patrika) is available. However, there is no clear system for recording the rights of each apartment independently and uniformly across the state,” said Bawankule.
An amendment will be made to the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966, regarding preparation and maintenance of records of rights and registers for apartments in buildings.
First, a main record of the building and common areas will be prepared, followed by a separate supplementary record for each apartment.
In urban survey areas, D-1 is proposed for the building and D-2 for each apartment, while in rural and other areas, I-A (Village Form 7-K) is proposed for the building and I-B (Village Form 7-D) for the apartment.
This will include the apartment number, holder’s name, sanctioned area, related rights and encumbrances, building area in the sanctioned plan, and open space. Each apartment will be assigned a unique identification number.
Entries will be based on the verification of the sanctioned building plan, relevant certificates, and registered documents.
For new projects, it is proposed to make entries based on the commencement certificate issued by the competent planning authority, and for existing buildings, based on the occupancy certificate and registered documents.
The landowner, promoter, developer, apartment holder, or an authorized person of a society/body can apply. Depending on the case, the original record of rights, sanctioned plan, relevant certificates, conveyance or deemed conveyance deed, and registered documents of apartment rights will be required.
Apartment-wise recording is proposed for bank loans, mortgages, court restrictions, and government dues, following the applicable procedure and based on orders or reliable information from the competent authority.
An integrated system will be developed for applications, data collection, necessary site verification, rectification of deficiencies, record approval, and distribution of digitally signed cards. Time-bound digital exchange of information is proposed among the Registration and Stamps Department, and others.

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola says his next coaching role will be with a national team after turning down the chance to take charge of Italy this year.
Guardiola held talks with the Italian Football Federation but said the offer arrived when he felt it was the right time to take a break from management.
“I talked with them, and it was an honor,” Guardiola said in an interview with his former Barcelona teammate Romario on Tuesday.
“It was one of the greatest honors I’ve had, that they thought of me to coach Italy. But it came at a time when I needed to stop.
“If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted. But when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom I love dearly, reached out, it was at a point where I simply had to stop.”
Guardiola left City at the end of last season after a decade in charge in which he won six Premier League titles, including an unprecedented four in succession, as well as three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League.
The Spaniard said the demands of nearly two decades in club management made a break necessary.
“I don’t know how long I’ll be away,” Guardiola said. “Right now I feel very well. But if I return to football one day, it will be when my stomach tells me it’s the right time.”

7 gadgets that’ll instantly upgrade your Thanksgiving feast
These tools will make turkey day just a little easier.

Thanksgiving is supposed to be a time for rest, relaxation and appreciating all the good things that have happened to you over the past year. However, there's no denying that it's also a ton of work for whoever is in charge of preparing your Thanksgiving meal. Not only do you have to consider the cooking itself, there's all the other things that come with making a holiday feast like choosing the right recipes, gathering all the ingredients and scheduling which dishes need to be cooked at what time so everything is ready together. And all that doesn't even include managing anyone who feels like helping, which can turn into its own logistical issue.
So to help smooth out the chaos that is holiday cooking, we've put together a collection of essential cooking gadgets that can save you time and take some of the stress out of preparing your Thanksgiving bounty.
A sharp knife
Most people probably wouldn't consider a knife to be very techy, and for most blades that sentiment rings true. But on days like Thanksgiving where you're going to be doing a ton of chopping, cutting, slicing and more, it can't hurt to have a little extra help. And then there's the turkey, because it isn't going to carve itself. Furthermore, if you want your bird to look anything like it does in cooking videos with those neat, super clean slices, you're going to need a sharp tool to get there.
For cooking nerds who like to geek out about the science of sharpness, one of my favorite knives on the market right now is the Seattle Ultrasonics C-200. In addition to just being a really nice knife featuring a three-layer san mai blade made out of Japanese AUS-10 steel, inside its handle there's a motor that vibrates the knife 30,000 times per second. While the oscillations are so small that you can't actually feel it shaking, those vibrations increased the knife's effective sharpness by up to 50 percent. It excels at delicate foods like tomatoes that often like to stick to the side of your blade, but also denser things like potatoes and meat, which obviously includes turkey. The C-200 even comes with an IP65 rating for dust and water resistance, so there's no worry about ruining its electronics with an errant splash. And if you opt for the wireless charging tile, you'll never have to worry about keeping its battery topped up. Granted, starting at $399, it certainly isn't cheap, but that price is very much in the same range as other premium chef knives from big name companies like Shun, Wusthoff and others.
Alternatively, if you want a dedicated gadget for helping you carve a turkey, you can always turn to more traditional electric knives like those from Cusinart, NutriChef, Hamilton Beach and more. Admittedly, these types of knives aren't nearly as pretty as blades like the C200 and the need to plug them in makes them harder to use on an everyday basis. But if you want a relatively easy and affordable way to make serving your Thanksgiving turkey go a bit more smoothly, a classic electric knife is definitely worth a look.
A meat thermometer
Even if you prefer side dishes like mashed potatoes, stuffing or a green bean casserole, there's no denying that the turkey is the star of Thanksgiving dinner. And if you want it to come out just right, you need a decent thermometer. Not having one is basically gambling that you get lucky with your timing and the bird turns out well. That said, there are a range of options, from simple digital sticks like the affordable ThermoPop 2 to fancy probe thermometers like the second-gen model from Combustion Inc.
Basic options require a bit more work as you can't leave them in the bird while it's in the oven, whereas more expensive versions have wireless support that allows you to leave them inside the turkey as it cooks. Some options like those from Combustion Inc. even account for carry-over cooking, which is when the temperature of the food continues to rise even after you take it out of the oven. You just need to decide how much you want to spend and what kind of features you really want. One of my more affordable favorites is the Sense from Chef IQ, which offers a great balance between price and performance. Just don't be a fool and try to rely strictly on the little pop-out thermometers that sometimes come with the bird, as those aren't known for their accuracy or precision.
An air fryer
A big issue during Thanksgiving is not having enough room in your oven for everything that needs to be baked or roasted. One easy solution to this is turning to an air fryer, which works almost exactly like the convection function on an oven, but in a smaller volume that's faster to heat and sometimes offers better air circulation. Another really nice thing about air fryers is that they can be quite affordable, with name brand models like the Instant Pot Vortex or the Ninja Air Fryer Pro, both of which are currently going for as little as $80.
Upgrading to more expensive fryers like the Philips 3000 can give you more capacity, while even pricier options like the Wonder Oven Pro from Our Place have as many as eight different functions for things like baking, roasting, dehydrating, proofing and more. And perhaps the best thing is that when the holidays are over, you can easily move these into your pantry, closet or garage and reclaim some of your precious kitchen counter space.
A digital scale
A good digital scale falls in the same general camp as a decent thermometer and there isn't an experienced baker that would be caught dead without one. They're super easy to use and in my opinion, they are a staple of any well-equipped kitchen. You can just plop a mixing bowl on top, zero out the scale and then add ingredients in as needed while you get precise measurements, which can be especially critical for baked goods and confections. OXO makes a very nice and rather affordable digital scale that starts at around $65, but you can find cheaper options from well-known brands like KitchenAid for barely more than $20.
A blender or immersion blender
A lot of people think blenders are big, bulky contraptions that make a ton of noise and take up too much room in your kitchen. And while the most powerful ones often are, they don't need to be, as there are affordable options that aren't much bigger than a teapot like these ones from Magic Bullet and Ninja. Regardless, they are great for making a post-dinner milkshake or a lovely fall-inspired soup (butternut squash anyone?).
Alternatively, you can opt for an immersion blender (aka a hand blender), which can do much of the same functions as a big countertop model, but gives you even greater control and the ability to blend things directly on the stovetop using the pots you already own. This can make them better choices for whipping up sauces like hollandaise (which is delicious when poured over roasted asparagus), mayonnaise or even a classic cranberry sauce to go with your turkey. I prefer cordless options like those from KitchenAid as they have more than enough battery life to complete multiple dishes and the lack of a wire makes them super easy to use. But if your budget is tight, traditional cabled options are totally fine too and often a more affordable choice.
A food processor
Even for people like me who prefer to chop things by hand, a food processor can be an incredible time saver during the holidays. Not only do they make quick minces of veggies, they can also be used to grate cheese, shred things like potatoes (for an easy Thanksgiving hash), or whip up dips like salsa. Some options like the Cusinart Mini Food processor are stupendously cheap at under $30, while pricer models like the Ninja Professional Plus Food Processor come with a bunch of attachments to handle all sorts of dishes.
A sous vide machine
Cooking food in a water bath might seem like an unnecessarily complex thing to do for the holidays, but it can actually save you time and effort. A good sous vide machine like those from Anova or Breville allow you to set an exact temperature and hold it there almost indefinitely. This allows you to cook things like meat with precision, so there's no worrying about if something is going to come out medium-rare or well-done.
And even on Thanksgiving where turkey is the main protein, you can still use a sous vide machine to make dishes like superb rosemary mashed potatoes or luscious glazed carrots. Some models even come with Wi-Fi, so you can start and set them remotely using your phone. On top of that, all they need to function is an outlet, so a sous vide machine can be a great option for people with small kitchens or a limited number of burners on their stove.

Quick Answer
Ente Photos is a privacy-focused Google Photos alternative offering 10GB of free storage, end-to-end encryption, open-source code, selective album backups, cross-platform access, easy photo imports, collaborative sharing, and on-device AI features like face recognition and Magic Search.
When we think about a dedicated photo app, we instantly remember Google Photos or the default gallery on our phone. We do not have many trustworthy options. That’s when I came across Ente. Ente is a dedicated photo app available as a standalone app to install on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Linux operating systems.
Is Ente the real challenger to the Google Photos app? Can we replace the gallery on our phones with Ente? Let’s find out.
Table of Contents
Features That Make Ente a Worthy Photo App
Ente has some exciting features that really make it stand out from the few others available. Here’s what makes it worthy.
Generous Free (Forever) Storage Plan
Ente offers a 10GB free storage plan for your photos and videos. Ente claims the plan is free forever. 10GB of free cloud storage dedicated to photos and video backup seems a good deal. That too without any ads.
Google offers 15GB of free storage space for each Google account. There is no dedicated storage space for the Google Photos app. As Google’s free storage is tied to all Google products as a whole, Ente’s 10GB looks big.
If you exhaust the generous free space on Ente, you can upgrade to a paid plan that offers storage starting from 50GB to 2TB for a monthly or annual subscription.
End-to-End Encrypted Backups
The photos and videos you back up on Ente are end-to-end encrypted by default. Ente claims they never use our data to train their models or spy on us.
The photos we back up via Google Photos are not end-to-end encrypted. Google may use our data to train their AI models, serve us customized ads, etc. You can prevent Google from using your data to show you personalized ads, but they can read your data. That’s where Ente succeeds.
The backup is end-to-end encrypted with keys before it leaves our device. The encryption keys are derived from our password using advanced key derivation functions. That means only the password you set can decrypt the data.
As the source code of Ente is publicly audited, the trust factor improves. When I tried to sign up on Ente, it provided me with a recovery key or the master key that I can use in case I lose my password.
The encryption process involves only us, the users, and they can never access the data. Even in the unfortunate event of a data breach, our data can remain safe as it is end-to-end encrypted.
Fully Open-Source Platform
Ente’s entire codebase for photos and its other apps is available for public audit on GitHub with more than 29k stars. The stars do not necessarily mean the project is good, but they give some form of trust.
The internet rewards the sensation. If someone had found a mismatch between Ente’s tall claims and the code, they surely would have flagged it and made an issue out of it.
Backup of User-Selected Albums
When you give permissions for Google Photos on our device, it backs up all the available albums, photos, and videos. We cannot select or ignore certain albums.
Ente, on the other hand, gives users the option to select which albums to back up. The albums that we choose not to back up are ignored by Ente as well. I loved this feature personally, as a lot of unnecessary data gets uploaded and wastes storage space. We can also customize the albums for backup anytime.
Easy Accessibility on All Platforms
Ente Photo has an app for every major operating system. We can install its app on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms. If we do not want to install the app, we can use it on the web through Ente.com.
Import Data From Google and Apple
Just download the Google Takeout that only has Google Photos data, import it into the Ente desktop app, and you are all set. It’s that simple to import data from Google Photos.
If you are an Apple user, just install the Ente app on your mobile device. Ente will read the data directly from your iCloud library and import it.
If you have iCloud shared albums, select the photos you want to import into the Ente app, and then save them to your device library for Ente to read them automatically.
Better Sharing and Collaboration Features
Ente Photo app provides us with three ways to share albums with others. You can share with a person on Ente, create a public link and share it with non-Ente users, or create a collaborative link to let non-Ente users add photos without an Ente account.
This does not put pressure on non-users to create an Ente account before collaborating with Ente albums, unlike the Google Photos app.
On-Device Machine Learning Features
There are a few machine learning-based features, like Magic Search, where you can search for photos with descriptions of how you remember them, Face Recognition, Memory Lane, Map and Location, and Jump to Date. These are all the latest advances in AI features.
To protect and maintain your privacy, all the machine learning happens on your device itself and is never sent to Ente’s servers. The machine learning feature is not enabled by default. You have to enable it manually and choose to disable it whenever you need to do so.
Is Ente Photos safe to use?
Yes, the Ente Photos app is safe to use to back up your photos and videos. It provides end-to-end encryption based on your password, and only your password can decrypt the data. Once you forget your password and also lose the recovery key they provided, you may never get to access the backup. The entire codebase of the Ente Photos app is available for public audit on GitHub.
How do I transfer photos from Google Photos to Ente?
You can transfer photos from Google Photos to the Ente Photos app in two ways. You can either download Google Photos data from Google Takeout, or download the entire library from the Google Photos app and drop it into the Ente Photos desktop app. It will read the data and import it to back it up safely.

After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.
In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”
“Our recent terms update was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”
Aaron Meshon, a longtime professional illustrator and Etsy seller, told Ars that even though the company had dialed back its AI language somewhat, the changes were mere “sugar coating.”
He said he still plans on shutting down his 15-year-old Etsy store on December 1.
“I would say I’m losing 20 percent of my yearly income,” he said. “It’s a few mortgage payments.”
He noted that Etsy’s announcement also seems to be rather tone-deaf, given that many retailers make a substantial portion of their annual revenue in the run-up to the end-of-year holiday season.

Cairo, Nov 26: A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.
The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the Health Ministry.
The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the Health Ministry.
At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video shows firefighters working to put out the fire spreading amongst the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.
Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The Public Prosecutor's office said DNA investigations were underway to identify the victims.
Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene himself. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further. Initial statements said 25 people were injured, but that figure was later revised to 21.
Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.
In January, 21 people were killed, and 16 were injured in a massive multi-car pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network’s build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket.
The launch was an important rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the company seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA’s Vulcan rocket, Amazon’s primary launch provider. Now, an Amazon official tells Ars it is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches the company has purchased from SpaceX, which also owns the Starlink satellite network that Amazon seeks to dethrone.
The next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now planned for December, Amazon said, moved forward from its previous launch date next year. Several more Falcon 9s are scheduled to launch Amazon Leo satellites in rapid succession after the December flight.
Winners and losers
Amazon cast a wide net when it started signing deals for launch services five years ago, securing rides on 108 flights with every available medium- or heavy-lift rocket in the West to place a fleet of 3,232 satellites into low-Earth orbit. As of Tuesday, Amazon and its launch partners have completed 17 of those flights, with one mission failure.
Amazon executives initially bought up capacity from US-based United Launch Alliance, Europe’s Arianespace, and Blue Origin. Nearly all of those launch contracts depended on rockets still in development: ULA’s Vulcan, Europe’s Ariane 6, and Blue Origin’s New Glenn.
Each launch vehicle faced development delays, as all new rockets do. New Glenn has been grounded since May after an explosion on Blue Origin’s launch pad in Florida. ULA’s Vulcan will be sidelined for months after misfiring during a mission with Amazon satellites on November 15.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Thursday (November 26, 2026) inaugurated, through video conferencing from the Secretariat in Chennai, 148 newly constructed houses at a cost of ₹8.52 crore at the Sri Lankan Tamil Rehabilitation Camp at Pambar Dam in Krishnagiri district.

Minister for Welfare of Non-Resident Tamils K. Thennarasu, Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, Secretary, Public and Rehabilitation Department, A. Sundaravalli, were among those present.
Dignitaries call on CM Vijay
In a separate development, High Commissioner of Australia to India Philip Green, Australian Consul General in Chennai Silai Zaki, and Deputy Consul General at the Australian Consulate General in Chennai Cameron Noble, among others, called on the Chief Minister.
Deborah Thiagarajan, founder and director of Dakshina Chitra; Maya Thiagarajan, managing trustee; and Sharath Nambiar, director of the museum, also met Mr. Vijay.

10 terrorists, 60 hours, 166 dead: The 26/11 night that still haunts Mumbai
Ten armed men unleashed a coordinated assault on Mumbai, turning several parts of the city into battlegrounds and leaving a wound India has never forgotten.
Mumbai never sleeps, but on the night of November 26, 2008, it was jolted awake by terror. Ten armed men unleashed a coordinated assault on the city, turning the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Oberoi-Trident and other landmarks into battlegrounds and leaving a wound India has never forgotten.
The gunmen, from Pakistan-based terror group Lashkar-e-Taiba, also brought carnage to Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST) railway station, the bustling Leopold Café and Nariman House. For the next 60 hours, the country’s financial capital lived through chaos and astonishing courage, as National Security Guard (NSG) commandos went in to hunt down and eliminate the terrorists.
By the time the guns fell silent, nine of the 10 terrorists were dead. The tenth, Ajmal Kasab, was in custody. But, what was devastating was that 166 people were killed, including 20 security personnel and 26 foreign nationals. The brazen attack tore through thousands of families and pushed India-Pakistan ties to the brink. It also led India to overhaul its counter-terrorism response. But above all, it led to the formation of India's first dedicated federal counter-terrorism agency, the National Investigation Agency (NIA).
Deep Dive
Also Read | 18 years later, 6 key conspirators of 26/11 attacks operate freely in Pakistan
What happened on the night of 26/11?
According to investigators, the 10 terrorists set sail from Karachi on November 21, loaded with assault rifles, grenades and explosives. As they neared the Indian coast on November 23, they hijacked an Indian fishing boat and killed four crew members. They only spared the captain, so he could steer them to Mumbai. Around 7 km off the Mumbai coast, he was killed too.
Then-home minister P Chidambaram told the Lok Sabha that on the evening of November 26, the terrorists finally landed near Budhwar Park, Coloba in Mumbai. They came ashore between 8:00 to 8:30 pm and broke into teams. The NIA submitted a report to the Supreme Court, saying that at about 9:15 pm, the first pair, Ajmal Kasab and Ismail Khan, walked into the packed CST station and opened fire on the crowd. When the shooting ended, at least 58 people were dead and more than 100 wounded.
The violence quickly spread across south Mumbai, with indiscriminate firing and bomb blasts across the city. At the Leopold Café, a haunt of locals and tourists alike, two gunmen launched an attack with grenades and gunfire at diners and killed 11 people, the NIA said. Timer bombs hidden in two taxis near the café blew up, killing five others, the investigations revealed. Another group blasted a petrol pump and laid siege to a Jewish outreach centre at Nariman House, where six Israelis lost their lives, reports said.
Also Read | Congress gave clean chit to Pakistan after 26/11 due to vote bank politics, BJP alleges
At around 9:45 pm, the terrorists shifted their targets to the Taj Mahal Palace and Tower Hotel. Two of them entered the lobby and opened fire on the guests and staff; two others began hurling grenades at the crowd.
Around the same time, a separate group of terrorists stormed the Oberoi-Trident Hotel. They opened fire on guests, set off explosives and took hostages. At least 35 people were killed inside the hotel, the NIA told the Supreme Court.
A long battle
The Mumbai Police were the first to respond. They rushed in to evacuate civilians while the attacks raged.
Kasab and Ismail Khan, meanwhile, slipped out of CST and into the nearby Cama Hospital at around 11 pm. The investigators said the hospital staff saw them coming and locked the patients' wards. A police team went in after them and fought a fierce battle on the upper floors. Two policemen were killed. The two terrorists then fled the hospital and lay in wait in a dark lane outside. There they ambushed a police vehicle and killed six policemen, including Mumbai Anti-Terrorism Squad chief Hemant Karkare, Additional Commissioner Ashok Kamte and police officer Vijay Salaskar.
The two terrorists subsequently hijacked a police vehicle but were soon intercepted by a team. In the ensuing gunfight, Khan was killed; police officer Tukaram Omble also lost his life in an attempt to disarm Kasab, before he was taken into custody.
Also Read | 'I will handle them': The story of 26/11 hero Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan
The Taj Mahal Palace, however, was still under siege. Past midnight, a massive blast tore through the hotel and fire swept up into its iconic central dome. The landmark of more than a century burned against the night sky as the country watched.
Final assault
There was still no end in sight. The police had surrounded the Taj, yet the heavily armed gunmen inside kept firing and held hostages as fires raged through the building. A small team of Indian Navy marine commandos was the first to go in after the terrorists, and they held them off through the night. On the morning of November 27, commandos from the National Security Guards, who were flown in from Delhi, took over. They launched Operation Black Tornado, storming the Taj, the Oberoi-Trident and Nariman House to free the hostages and hunt down the attackers.
For two more days, gunfire, explosions and fires shook the besieged buildings. On November 28, the commandos finally cleared the Oberoi-Trident and rescued hundreds of hostages. Later that day, they secured the Nariman House, after fast-roping onto its roof from a helicopter. All attackers at the two sites were dead.
The next morning, the commandos secured the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, killing the last terrorists. Around 36 people were killed in the three-day siege, and several portions of the premises were destroyed by fires and explosions.
Eighteen years on, the scars of 26/11 have not faded. The scale of the carnage, the cold precision of the planning and the sheer devastation remain seared into India's memory. The attacks still cast a long shadow over India's relations with Pakistan, and they forced a sweeping overhaul of how the country guards its shores and fights terror.

On Nov. 23, Nvidia announced the tech company had reinstated cofounder Jensen Huang as president and CEO. In the hours that followed, people shared an alleged screenshot appearing to show that U.S. President Donald Trump had shared an altered image of Huang on Truth Social.
That altered image showed Huang standing in Trump's place at the site of the Butler, Pennsylvania, assassination attempt in July 2024. A flag bearing the Nvidia logo hangs on the right side. Huang's right hand — formerly Trump's pumped fist — holds a red bra, appearing to allude to Jensen Huang's affair with Chinese businesswoman and alleged government spy Alice Huang.
For example, people posted (archived) the purported screenshot from Trump's Truth Social account on Facebook (archived), Instagram (archived) and X (archived).
(@atrupar via X)
Snopes readers also emailed us to ask whether Trump actually shared the altered image.
In sum, this was true. The altered image showing Huang holding a red bra in the Butler assassination attempt photo appeared in a Nov. 23 post on Trump's Truth Social account (archived).
(@realDonaldTrump via Truth Social)
The fake image displays a watermark for the user @grandoldmemes, who previously posted the same meme on Instagram and X, with the latter displaying a label for parody content. The user acknowledged that Trump's account had reposted the image.
Snopes emailed the White House to ask why Trump reposted the fake image and will update this article if we receive further information.
Huang reinstated, Trump's investments
The user @grandoldmemes posted the inauthentic meme shortly after Nvidia, which dominates the market for computer chips used by artificial intelligence models, announced its board of directors had reinstated Jensen Huang. Huang resigned earlier in the month after news media outlets reported on his relationship with Alice Huang.
The New York Times reported on Nov. 23 that Trump, who holds investments in the chip maker — as confirmed in various public disclosures — directed Nvidia's effort to reinstate Huang.
Last week, Congress announced Jensen Huang voluntarily agreed to appear before three House committees. He will likely face scrutiny over the affair and reports of Nvidia's advanced chips being diverted to China.

At this Little Free Bakery in Austin, neighbors come for the pastries and stay for community connection
AUSTIN, Texas— When lines form in parks they're usually for the playground. Kids taking turns on slides. Runners waiting to get a drink from a water fountain. But the line that forms in the Bruning Green park in Austin's North Loop neighborhood happens only once a month, always on the first Sunday, and includes people of all ages. They're all here for Sarah Mason's bakery.
Unlike other bakeries in town where a pastry can run upwards of $7, everything here is free.
Mason's popup is one of countless Little Free Bakeries across the country. The idea is similar to Little Free Libraries, the small boxes that are often set up in front yards where passersby can leave or take a book as they please. Instead of books, it's baked goods that are up for grabs.
The bakers behind these Little Free Bakeries make everything from classic chocolate chip cookies to croissants all at no cost to their neighbors. Some have different reasons for starting than others, but what many inadvertently created is a space for their community to come together and get to know one another.
Mason started the Free Bakery North Loop last September when she was working on improving her technical pastry skills. She was handing out baked goods at her job as an office leasing representative for WeWork, but soon she had more than she could give away.
For her first free bakery, Mason made around 150 items, ranging from coconut chocolate chip cookies to bacon cheddar chive scones.
She thought people would happen upon the event as they were walking through the neighborhood. But just in case, she posted on social media. That post took off and since then there has always been a line.
"I have a friend who jokes that waiting in the line is the most fun part, because everyone's excited and talking about what they're going to get when they get to the front of the line and you can meet people," Mason said.
People love a free treat, but Mason said she is pleasantly surprised at how many people stick around and hang out.
"It was unexpected," she said. "My observation of other free bakeries, it's more of a grab and go situation. But because we were in this park, it felt like there was room to spread out and room for other activities. It became more of a community event than just a free pastry."
For people like Sara and J.R. Almanza, the event hearkens back to old Austin, a time before the tech boom when the skyline had fewer skyscrapers and when the pace of life felt slower and it was easier to strike up a conversation with strangers. After attending the free bakery once, the Almanzas decided to come back and enjoy the sense of community.
"Right now it seems like people are becoming more divided. It feels like everything's so polarizing these days," J.R. said. "There's so much out there to kind of distract us from meeting people and engaging with other people, that events like this are important because it brings people together."
That sense of community is part of what led Lanne Stauffer to create the very first Little Free Bakery in Seattle in 2021.
It all started in Seattle
Stauffer got the idea for a Little Free Bakery after she experienced a small act of kindness.
"We were still in the pandemic and the mood was scared and nobody was coming out of their houses and just a lot of fear in the air and there was a bouquet of flowers on my front step," Stauffer said.
Receiving those flowers created a shift in how she was feeling inside.
"Just the joy of finding that bouquet of flowers on my front step changed my day and I wanted to know what I could do to change other folks' day in the same way," she said.
But Stauffer isn't a florist. She's a baker. She thought of Little Free Libraries and asked her husband to build her a pick-up box.
"It gives me so much joy to bake for people," she said. "It's the way I say I love you, and so even if nobody came that day, just knowing I was baking for the community made me feel good."
That Tuesday, people did come though — and in an hour all 50 little apple pies were gone. By the time it was over, Stauffer decided she would do it again the following week.
It's been five years since then, and Stauffer has noticed a couple of things. Chocolate and lemon sweets are more popular than others. And the treats aren't the only reason people stop by.
"People are always grateful to have a place to come and meet their neighbors and have conversations often about what's going on in the news," she said. "We stand around and hug each other or laugh or cry, share our fears, and it's just added another gathering spot in our neighborhood."
Some neighbors even plan their weeks around the pastry drops.
Erin Creighton Tozier has lived in Seattle's Magnolia neighborhood for five years, but didn't know about the Stauffer's Little Free Bakery until a year ago.
"It's just like the anchor in our week," Creighton Tozier said. "I have a demanding job, but it's like a 3 p.m. calendar marker … a break in the day to get some fresh air. Even if it's raining, no matter the weather, like my dog and I go, we have a sweet treat, we chat with our neighbors."
To celebrate her neighbors coming out for five years, Stauffer baked a 5-foot-long white cake, with orange curd filling, a cardamom cream cheese frosting and a pomegranate molasses drizzle.
Her family helped decorate it with fall fruits before they put it out in the driveway.
"I have learned that folks need to feel connected and they can feel comforted by me just baking them something," she said.
The growing free bakery movement
It only took a couple months after Stauffer started the Little Free Bakery Seattle for another one to open up.
"Then it started to snowball from there, and I was having somebody reach out to me every month for a while opening a new little free bakery," Stauffer said. "I didn't know that I was starting a movement but that has been one of the biggest delights."
Now little free bakeries exist in Nashville, Tenn.; Salt Lake City, Utah; Fredericksburg, Va. and other cities.
Stauffer recently took a road trip to visit some of the other bakeries and collect stories and recipes from her fellow bakers for an upcoming book, The Little Free Bakery Book: Recipes for Sharing & Building Community, written with Jill Lightner.
Stauffer, like Mason in Austin, hopes that the movement continues to grow. "I think every neighborhood should have a little free bakery," Mason said.
In Austin, other free bakeries have popped up since Mason started hers. But the reach goes farther. In Chattanooga, Tenn., her sister plans to start a free bakery there.
"I think she just saw how much fun we're having here and thought that she wants a little slice of that in her own neighborhood," Mason said.

On anaemia in India and what the numbers tell us, women’s health, healthy eating for children, an update on infectious diseases and air pollution, and more
The biggest news this week in health care in India is the new anaemia figures published by the Union Health Ministry. It claimed that the rates of severe anaemia have dropped and mild anaemia dominated the population.
Let’s understand the context to this: The Centre decided to stop measuring anaemia as part of the National Family Health Survey, after its fifth edition, and decided instead to take up measuring anaemia and micronutrient deficiencies separately.
They said measuring anaemia in venous blood (blood drawn from the veins) would be a better indicator of anaemia to the more mass finger prick technique that NFHS used. Researchers would also use auto analysers to process the samples and this would give greater credibility to the data generated, and a more accurate picture of ground reality.
